Some post-upgrade symptoms come from identity and default changes rather than faults: security scanners reject the reported MySQL-compatible version string, which can be re-published via the server-version config (or tiup cluster edit-config plus reload -R tidb) - masking the real version, so cross-check the string when version-dependent behavior shifts. Notable default shifts include v5.1 setting tidb_analyze_version=2 (new statistics implementation) and tidb_partition_prune_mode=static (dynamic pruning off by default), security.enable-sem/tidb_enable_enhanced_security requiring a restart to change, cte_max_recursion_depth bounding recursive CTEs, and statement priority keywords (LOW_PRIORITY/HIGH_PRIORITY) being superseded by resource control - all of which change observed behavior without any fault. Some post-upgrade symptoms come from identity and default changes rather than faults: security scanners reject the reported MySQL-compatible version string, which can be re-published via the server-version config (or tiup cluster edit-config plus reload -R tidb) - masking the real version. Notable shifts: v5.1 set tidb_analyze_version=2 and tidb_partition_prune_mode=static (dynamic pruning off), and SEM requires a restart to change; v6.0 removed the stmt-summary.* config items in favor of SQL variables and flipped new_collations_enabled_on_first_bootstrap default to true (bootstrap-time only); v6.5.0 defaulted cost model version 2, outer-join reorder ON, metadata lock ON, fast reorg (ADD INDEX acceleration) ON, deprecated tidb_enable_amend_pessimistic_txn, and changed tidb_mem_quota_query to a session-level threshold for DML; v6.5.7 added performance.force-init-stats and switched TiFlash logger.level from debug to info (debug evidence disappears after upgrade); v7.3.0 made TiFlash pushdown MPP-only, so tidb_allow_mpp=OFF causes query errors after upgrade (set tidb_allow_tiflash_cop=ON to restore Cop plans); v7.6.0 raised the default TLS floor from 1.1 to TLS 1.2+ (old clients fail to connect), enabled Titan by default for new clusters with min-blob-size 32KB and zstd blob compression, and BR refuses full restore into a non-empty cluster (use --filter to force). Review these defaults before attributing new behavior to bugs.

nodes.name: Upgrade Interacting with Running ADD INDEX
nodes.content: Mechanism: upgrading the cluster while an ADD INDEX backfill is running can leave indexes inconsistent with the data, and rolling restarts have historically left DDLs stuck in the running state; ADD INDEX itself can also fail from TiDB memory exhaustion on large tables. Diagnosis: after an upgrade or rolling restart that overlapped a DDL, run ADMIN CHECK on the affected indexes and check the DDL job state rather than assuming the index is valid; for ADD INDEX OOM, correlate failure with table size and memory quota. Repair family: quiesce DDL jobs before upgrades (ADMIN SHOW DDL/DDL JOBS), re-run or repair the affected index (admin recover/cleanup index families) after verifying inconsistency, and stage large index builds with adequate memory.

nodes.name: Upgrade interruption recovery runbook
nodes.content: Mechanism: an interrupted upgrade leaves partially upgraded nodes; re-running tiup cluster upgrade restarts already-upgraded nodes, and stuck scenarios trace to plugin loading, kill -9 offline upgrades, or DDL owner changes on the concurrent-DDL table queue. Differential: find the failed operation and its audit-id with tiup cluster audit, and identify the stall cause from TiDB logs and recent node kills or owner changes. Remedies: (a) resume with tiup cluster replay <audit-id> to retry without restarting upgraded nodes; (b) restart the affected new-version TiDB node (avoid kill -9; wait about 2 minutes after a kill if unavoidable); (c) reserve --force only for emergencies since it skips leader eviction and ignores upgrade errors. Risks: --force on an online cluster causes direct restarts and hides failures; an unhealthy node aborts upgrades until manually repaired.

nodes.name: Vector Index Usage Semantics
nodes.content: HNSW vector indexes serve approximate KNN only when the query is ORDER BY distance-function ... LIMIT with exactly the same distance function as the index definition; a WHERE pre-filter executed before KNN defeats the index and degrades to a full scan. Rewrite filtered vector searches as a KNN subquery followed by an outer filter (accepting possibly fewer results), and verify with EXPLAIN that the index is chosen when vector queries are unexpectedly slow. HNSW vector indexes serve approximate KNN only when the query is ORDER BY distance-function ... LIMIT with exactly the same distance function as the index definition; a WHERE pre-filter executed before KNN defeats the index and degrades to a full scan. EXPLAIN shows annIndex: in the scan operator info when the index is used, and SHOW WARNINGS names the reason otherwise (wrong distance function, DESC order unsupported - ASC only - or a missing Top-K LIMIT); rewrite filtered searches as a KNN subquery with an outer filter.

nodes.name: Wait Time versus Process Time
nodes.content: Mechanism: among slow queries only those with large process_time actually pressure the cluster; statements with large wait_time and small process_time are victims queued behind real offenders. Discrimination: compare Cop_process/Cop_wait or process_time vs wait_time per slow entry, and check which TiKV instances the cop tasks hit. Fix family: optimize or throttle the high process_time statements first; victim statements recover once the offender is fixed, so do not tune them individually.

nodes.name: Window Function TopN Derivation
nodes.content: With tidb_opt_derive_topn=ON (off by default, v7.0+), TiDB rewrites outer filters on ROW_NUMBER() into a pushed-down TopN (executed on TiKV/TiFlash) instead of sorting the whole input, but only for ROW_NUMBER with filter operators < or <= and no PARTITION BY case differences to verify. If a window query still sorts everything, check the rule applies and that the rule is not blocklisted.

nodes.name: Workload Edge-Case Identification
nodes.content: Method for finding scenario-specific performance edge cases beyond baseline tuning: analyze query patterns and workload characteristics, monitor system metrics to localize bottlenecks, and gather application-team feedback on concrete issues; the combined evidence decides which targeted optimization applies.

nodes.name: Write and Commit Latency Breakdown
nodes.content: Mechanism: write duration decomposes into lock acquisition, prewrite, commit-ts retrieval, schema check, and commit PK; 1pc and async-commit skip most of the 2pc chain. Discrimination: high latch wait (acquire_pessimistic_lock) on a few TiKV instances means hot-Region lock conflicts, across all instances means application-level conflicts; large prewrite/commit segments point at Region count, Raft, or disk. Fix family: resolve conflicts (application redesign, hotspot dispersion), then tune the commit path once conflicts are excluded.

nodes.name: Write Conflict Diagnosis
nodes.content: Mechanism: two transactions write the same key and the later prewrite conflicts with the earlier one; with LazyUniquenessCheck a pessimistic transaction can still hit unique-index conflicts. Discrimination: ERROR 9007 with reason=LazyUniquenessCheck means pessimistic unique-check deferral; conflicts concentrated on few keys indicate hotspot rows or retry storms. Fix family: add application-level retry of the whole transaction, enable tidb_constraint_check_in_place_pessimistic to check eagerly, or reduce concurrent updates to the same keys; retries amplify load so watch QPS.

nodes.name: Write Conflict Mitigation
nodes.content: Mechanism: many transactions touching the same rows or adjacent keys serialize on locks and burn retries. Diagnosis: lock-conflict and retry errors, Key Visualizer bright spots on hot rows, transaction latency distribution. Fix family: spread hot write keys in schema design (shard or randomize identifiers where range scans are not required), keep transactions short and batched, and isolate conflicting workloads onto separate instances or resource groups. Risks: sharding keys changes access patterns and can hurt range queries; batching trades atomicity scope.

nodes.name: Optimistic Write Conflict Storm
nodes.content: Optimistic transactions buffer writes in TiDB memory and detect conflicts only at prewrite against start_ts, so concurrent updates to hot rows abort with write-conflict errors and retry entire transactions, inflating TiDB memory/CPU and latency exactly when contention is highest. Distinguish from pessimistic lock waits by write-conflict errors and retry counters instead of lock-wait timeouts; fix family: move contended paths to pessimistic mode or shrink transaction size, risk is losing optimistic-mode throughput and adding blocking.

nodes.name: Write Hotspot on Single Region
nodes.content: Small, frequently updated tables (counter-style) compress into a handful of KV pairs that land in one Region on one node, so their write path cannot use TiDB's scaling and additionally pays replication overhead - this is the mechanism behind TiDB underperforming a standalone MySQL on such workloads, and the diagnosis is a single-Region write hotspot rather than a fault. Remedies range from AUTO_RANDOM/shard-row-id-bits key scattering for insert-heavy tables to accepting the design limit for tiny hot tables.

nodes.name: Write Hotspot Mitigation
nodes.content: Mechanism: sequential row IDs or auto-increment integer keys funnel new writes into one Region and Raft group, capping write throughput. Diagnosis: Key Visualizer bright diagonal/ladder lines in write flow, Raftstore CPU skewed to one TiKV, and leader/peer distribution from TIKV_REGION_STATUS. Fix family: pre-split and scatter Regions (SPLIT TABLE ... REGIONS), SHARD_ROW_ID_BITS with PRE_SPLIT_REGIONS for _tidb_rowid tables, AUTO_RANDOM instead of AUTO_INCREMENT integer primary keys, or random binary UUID keys with a CLUSTERED PK; ensure scattering completes before intensive writes. Risks: SHARD_ROW_ID_BITS does not apply to clustered-primary-key tables and only affects new writes; random keys lose range-scan locality.

nodes.name: Write Hotspot Region Warm-Up
nodes.content: Mechanism: each new table starts as one Region, so even random-key writes concentrate on its single leader; after splits, new leaders may remain on the original store until PD redistributes leaders and migrates Regions to idle nodes. Diagnosis: per-TiKV raftstore CPU skew plus PD hotspot metrics confirm the concentration; this warm-up is normal but must be designed away for sustained high-concurrency writes. Fix family: pre-split/shape keys or wait out warm-up before benchmarking.

nodes.name: Wrong Index Decision Path
nodes.content: Mechanism: the optimizer picks an unexpected index from outdated or skewed statistics, cost miscalculation, engine choice, or function-pushdown limits. Discrimination: check statistics health first - low health means run ANALYZE; near-full health with equality queries points at Count-Min Sketch estimation; EXPLAIN FORMAT=verbose exposes cost differences between candidate plans; skewed distributions need ANALYZE options tuned. Fix family: refresh statistics, pin the plan with USE_INDEX hints or SQL Plan Management, isolate the engine (TiKV versus TiFlash) for the query, adjust pushdown blocklists for unsupported expressions, or add a new index when data distribution has changed.

nodes.name: Zone Label Locality Semantics
nodes.content: TiDB server labels, especially zone, drive txn-scope and follower-read locality: a missing or wrong zone label silently degrades reads to cross-zone or leader-only paths and raises latency. Check instance labels against the intended topology when read latency or txn_scope behavior is unexplained; the group label is reserved for TiDB Operator and should not be set manually.

nodes.name: Active Connections
nodes.content: Count of active client sessions per TiDB over time; abnormal readings are sessions piling up while individual statements wait (lock waits, stalled DDL) versus a fall from crashes or connection limits

nodes.name: CPU Usage
nodes.content: CPU utilization per TiDB/TiKV/PD node; sustained saturation on one TiKV while peers idle indicates a hotspot or skewed scheduling, while uniform saturation indicates load growth, expensive plans, or background tasks such as reorg DDL and backup

nodes.name: Disk I/O
nodes.content: Per-node disk I/O utilization, throughput and queue depth; on TiKV it covers both KV RocksDB reads/writes and Raft Engine WAL flushes, so a device with very high flushes/sec and %util signals WAL or storage saturation

nodes.name: Disk Usage
nodes.content: Used vs available storage per TiKV store as reported in store heartbeats; abnormal when growth outpaces data volume (e.g., GC blocked by a stalled log backup checkpoint) or when a store approaches capacity and PD stops placing peers on it

nodes.name: Lightning Progress
nodes.content: Overall and per-step (encode, sort, ingest, checksum, analyze) progress of a TiDB Lightning or IMPORT INTO job; abnormal readings are a stalled phase (engine files never closing, checksum failing) or progress far slower than the data volume warrants

nodes.name: Lightning Throughput
nodes.content: Import data rate of Lightning/IMPORT INTO; physical import typically reaches an order of magnitude more GiB/hour than logical import, so a physical-mode job running at logical-mode speed points to sorting, disk, or TiKV ingest bottlenecks

nodes.name: Lightning Workers
nodes.content: Concurrency of Lightning import workers/instances; abnormal readings are worker starvation (idle workers while others backlog) or saturation of the target cluster from too many parallel engines

nodes.name: Memory Usage
nodes.content: Per-node memory usage of TiDB/TiKV/PD processes; abnormal readings are TiDB memory climbing during large optimistic transactions (writes buffered in memory until commit) or TiKV block-cache and raft entries pressuring the host toward OOM

nodes.name: Network I/O
nodes.content: Host-level network traffic and errors on pipeline component nodes; bandwidth shortage shows up as retries and EOF errors in import/export/replication tools.

nodes.name: PD Leader Distribution
nodes.content: Distribution of PD leaders across instances, reflecting control-plane availability and placement.

nodes.name: PD Region Activity
nodes.content: Region scheduling and health activity derived from TiKV heartbeats: hot-region counts, pending/down peers, and leader/peer movement; abnormal readings are hot regions concentrated on one store or persistent pending and down peers

nodes.name: PD Region Inventory
nodes.content: Inventory of regions and peers from PD store/region heartbeats: leader counts, peer counts, region size and status per store; abnormal readings are leader or peer counts skewed to one store, or growing pending/down peer counts

nodes.name: Plan Cardinality Estimates
nodes.content: Estimated row counts in execution plans versus actual rows; abnormal readings are estimates off by orders of magnitude (skewed columns, hash collisions, stale stats), the signature of a mis-chosen index or join order

nodes.name: QPS
nodes.content: Queries per second served by TiDB nodes, the headline throughput measure; abnormal readings are a plateau or drop while client load persists, often caused by hotspots, resource saturation, or background tasks such as reorg DDL and backup

nodes.name: Query Latency
nodes.content: End-to-end SQL latency per TiDB (typically as duration percentiles); abnormal readings are sustained percentile jumps or long-tail growth caused by lock waits, plan regressions, resource saturation, or topology-induced network round trips such as cross-AZ leader placement

nodes.name: Resource Group Throttle
nodes.content: Indicates resource groups being throttled at their RU or CPU quotas; abnormal readings are groups pinned at quota with queued work, showing up as latency rise confined to that group's queries

nodes.name: Resource Group Usage
nodes.content: Real-time Request Unit consumption total and per resource group, plus TiDB/TiKV CPU usage and TiKV IO MBps against configured quotas; abnormal readings are one group consuming far above its share and crowding others

nodes.name: Statistics State
nodes.content: Freshness and health of optimizer statistics (histograms, Count-Min Sketch/Top-N); abnormal readings are stale or missing stats, or estimate-versus-actual divergence from CMS hash collisions, which flip index and join-order choices and regress latency

nodes.name: TiCDC Progress
nodes.content: Changefeed replication checkpoint/progress for TiCDC pipelines; abnormal readings are a checkpoint that stalls or falls further behind the current ts, indicating capture, sort, or downstream sink bottlenecks and enlarging the data-loss window if the primary fails

nodes.name: TiCDC Sink
nodes.content: TiCDC downstream sink write throughput and latency; abnormal readings are sink errors, flush latency spikes, or throughput far below upstream write rate, which accumulates changefeed lag

nodes.name: Transaction Commit Activity
nodes.content: Transaction commit rate and duration reflecting two-phase commit plus Raft replication health; elevated commit latency with retries points to write conflicts or oversized transactions, and stalls point to Raft or storage slowness

nodes.name: Workload Profile
nodes.content: Composition of database time by SQL type and phase (get token/parse/compile/execute), by KV request kind (prewrite/commit green, reads blue, pessimistic lock red, TSO wait dark brown, TiFlash MPP purple) and by source (external vs internal such as DDL or auto-analyze); abnormal readings are large non-execution or non-blue/green areas revealing lock conflicts, TSO stalls, or internal task pressure

nodes.name: Backup Replication
nodes.content: Fault class around data replication and backup pipelines (binlog Pump/Drainer, downstream apply, checkpoints).

nodes.name: Backup and Restore
nodes.content: Fault classes around BR snapshot backup, log backup and PITR competing with or blocking normal workload

nodes.name: Bulk Import
nodes.content: Fault class around physical/logical data import: prechecks, key conflicts, checkpoint state, online interference, and replication pipeline compatibility.

nodes.name: Capacity
nodes.content: Storage and resource capacity boundaries, including free-space envelopes and headroom.

nodes.name: Cluster Maintenance
nodes.content: Fault class around planned maintenance: upgrades, rolling restarts, blue-green cutovers, component patching, and TiUP-managed state.

nodes.name: Concurrency
nodes.content: Knowledge about concurrency control, parallel execution degrees, and scheduling of queries.

nodes.name: Data Consistency
nodes.content: Tag for fault classes where data correctness is at risk, such as duplicate keys, constraint violations, replication divergence, or lost versions.

nodes.name: Data Import
nodes.content: Bulk data import and migration paths such as physical import, including checkpoint and capacity concerns.

nodes.name: Data Lifecycle
nodes.content: Fault class around automated row expiry and periodic cleanup (TTL attributes, TTL job scheduling and throughput).

nodes.name: Data Migration
nodes.content: Fault classes around DM/TiCDC/Lightning data pipelines lagging, pausing, or competing with the cluster

nodes.name: Data Pipeline
nodes.content: Bulk data movement into and out of TiDB: import/export (Lightning, Dumpling), backup/restore (BR), and replication (DM, TiCDC) tooling and their failure classes.

nodes.name: Data Replication
nodes.content: Knowledge about replicating data out of TiDB via CDC, binlog, and related pipelines.

nodes.name: Disaster Recovery
nodes.content: Failover, DR replication modes, fencing, and lossy recovery operations.

nodes.name: GC and MVCC
nodes.content: Knowledge about garbage collection, MVCC versions, and space reclamation.

nodes.name: HTAP Columnar Replica
nodes.content: Fault class around TiFlash columnar replicas: corruption, replica placement, scale-in rules, and replica availability.

nodes.name: Index Selection
nodes.content: Knowledge about how the optimizer picks indexes and how index design affects plans.

nodes.name: I/O Performance
nodes.content: Covers disk and storage IO topics: write stalls, compaction and flush pressure, WAL/Raft log write latency, and read/write amplification.

nodes.name: Memory Management
nodes.content: Memory quotas, spilling, and instance-level memory control for queries, plans, and transactions.

nodes.name: Partition Pruning
nodes.content: Knowledge about partitioned tables, pruning modes, and partition-level statistics.

nodes.name: Placement
nodes.content: Knowledge about data placement policies, placement rules, and replica location control.

nodes.name: Plan Management
nodes.content: Controlling and stabilizing optimizer plan choices through hints, bindings, baseline capturing and evolution, and plan caching.

nodes.name: Query Performance
nodes.content: Covers SQL latency, plan quality, and execution efficiency topics: slow queries, plan selection and regression, index usage, and optimizer behavior.

nodes.name: Region Hotspot
nodes.content: Load imbalance concentrated on a small key range or single Region leader/store

nodes.name: Region Scheduling
nodes.content: Covers PD scheduling of Regions: balance, hot-region scheduling, merge/split, and scheduling limits that govern cluster load distribution.

nodes.name: Resource Control
nodes.content: Tag for resource group fault classes: RU throttling, capacity calibration, and workload isolation.

nodes.name: Security and Privileges
nodes.content: Fault class around account management, privilege propagation, login failures, and access control (including resource-group administration rights).

nodes.name: Statistics Health
nodes.content: Freshness and accuracy of optimizer statistics that drive cardinality estimation.

nodes.name: Storage Housekeeping
nodes.content: Tag for GC and MVCC housekeeping fault classes: space reclamation lag, GC safe point conflicts, and version accumulation.

nodes.name: TiFlash Execution
nodes.content: Semantic tag grouping columnar-replica and MPP execution knowledge: replica readiness, plan selection, memory spilling, and isolation-read engine control.

nodes.name: Traffic Management
nodes.content: Fault class around client traffic paths: proxies, load balancers, session migration, connection lifetime, and rolling restarts.

nodes.name: Transactions and MVCC
nodes.content: Transaction lifecycle, MVCC versions, GC retention and locking behavior.

nodes.name: Workload Isolation
nodes.content: Fault class around isolating background and tenant workloads from foreground traffic (service scope, resource groups, task scheduling).

nodes.name: ADMIN CHECK TABLE
nodes.content: Verify data-index consistency for a table or index with ADMIN CHECK TABLE/INDEX; failures return count or value mismatches pinpointing the inconsistent index.

attributes.sql_template: ADMIN CHECK TABLE <table>;

nodes.name: ADMIN CHECK SQL
nodes.content: ADMIN CHECK TABLE and ADMIN CHECK INDEX verify that row data and index entries agree for a table or a single index, used both for scheduled verification and as the confirmation step of an inconsistency investigation.

attributes.sql_template: ADMIN CHECK TABLE db.t; ADMIN CHECK INDEX db.t idx_name;

nodes.name: Admin Cleanup Index
nodes.content: Remove redundant or stray index entries that reference no valid row with ADMIN CLEANUP INDEX after inconsistency is confirmed.

attributes.sql_template: ADMIN CLEANUP INDEX <db.table> <index_name>;

nodes.name: Admin Recover Index
nodes.content: Rebuild inconsistent index data from row records with ADMIN RECOVER INDEX; it runs single-threaded and is not atomic, so re-execute until success and confirm with ADDED_COUNT/SCAN_COUNT and ADMIN CHECK INDEX.

attributes.sql_template: ADMIN RECOVER INDEX <db.table> <index_name>; ADMIN CHECK INDEX <db.table> <index_name>;

nodes.name: ADMIN SHOW DDL JOBS
nodes.content: SQL statement that shows the current DDL owner and running DDL jobs, used to correlate workload impact with reorg DDL activity

attributes.sql_template: ADMIN SHOW DDL JOBS WHERE JOB_ID = <id>;

nodes.name: ADMIN SHOW SLOW
nodes.content: Retrieve recent or top slow query records kept in TiDB memory (ADMIN SHOW SLOW recent N / top [internal|all] N) with duration, digest, and timing details.

attributes.sql_template: ADMIN SHOW SLOW top 10;

nodes.name: Manual ANALYZE
nodes.content: Run ANALYZE after large batch updates or imports and whenever plans look suboptimal; TiDB also auto-corrects statistics it detects as inconsistent with estimates, and ANALYZE TABLE t PARTITION p scopes collection to partitions.

attributes.sql_template: ANALYZE TABLE <table> [INDEX <idx>[,<idx>...]] [WITH <n> BUCKETS] [WITH <n> TOPN];

nodes.name: Execution Plan Binding Verification
nodes.content: Verify restored SQL bindings with SHOW GLOBAL BINDINGS, deduplicate builtin_pseudo_sql_for_bind_lock rows in mysql.bind_info, and force reload with ADMIN RELOAD BINDINGS.

attributes.sql_template: SHOW GLOBAL BINDINGS; SELECT count(*) FROM mysql.bind_info WHERE original_sql = 'builtin_pseudo_sql_for_bind_lock'; ADMIN RELOAD BINDINGS;

nodes.name: Binlog Checkpoint Query
nodes.content: Read the Drainer replication checkpoint commit-ts from tidb_binlog.checkpoint to determine resume position and divergence window.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM tidb_binlog.checkpoint;

nodes.name: Binlog status SQL
nodes.content: TiDB SQL view of binlog state: SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'log_bin' (0 = enabled), SHOW PUMP STATUS and SHOW DRAINER STATUS for node state, and CHANGE PUMP/DRAINER TO NODE_STATE for abnormal-state repair only.

attributes.sql_template: SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'log_bin'; SHOW PUMP STATUS; SHOW DRAINER STATUS; CHANGE PUMP TO NODE_STATE='paused' FOR NODE_ID '<node>';

nodes.name: binlogctl
nodes.content: binlogctl inspects and manipulates Pump/Drainer node state stored in PD: pumps/drainers to list state, pause-*/offline-* for planned stops and removal, update-* only to correct stale state after abnormal exits.

nodes.name: br backup Control
nodes.content: tiup br backup full/db/table runs snapshot backups (db/table subsets, --filter table filters) with --ratelimit bounding impact and optional --backupts for a historical snapshot timestamp; schedule full backups periodically and pair with a log-backup task for PITR. tiup br backup full/db/table runs snapshot backups (db/table subsets, --filter table filters using db.tbl patterns with fnmatch wildcards *, ?, [a-z], [!a-z]) with --ratelimit bounding impact and optional --backupts for a historical snapshot timestamp; schedule full backups periodically and pair with a log-backup task for PITR.

nodes.name: BR Log Backup Task Control
nodes.content: tiup br log provides start/status/pause/resume/stop (stop deletes task metadata) and truncate (deletes restored-prefix log data from storage) plus metadata for the log directory; pause/resume is the safe way to relieve pressure without losing the task, while truncate is required before PITR can drop old restore points.

nodes.name: BR Restore Task Control
nodes.content: Run and monitor BR restore tasks (restore point / restore full) through the cluster management tool, checking the success summary ranges and progress output.

nodes.name: Business Invariant Verification
nodes.content: Verify business row counts, deterministic aggregates, and table checksums to confirm a restore or import reached terminal success.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM <db.table>; ADMIN CHECKSUM TABLE <db.table>;

nodes.name: TiCDC Redo Log Apply
nodes.content: Apply buffered redo logs to the secondary cluster to reach a transaction-consistent state before admitting it as primary. All TiCDC processes must have exited before running redo apply, and the sink must be MySQL-compatible; redo is enabled per changefeed with consistent level eventual plus storage, max-log-size, and flush-interval settings.

nodes.name: Changefeed Status Query
nodes.content: Query changefeed state, checkpoint, and sink errors with cdc cli changefeed list/query or the corresponding status tables.

nodes.name: Checkpoint Storage Inspection
nodes.content: Inspect checkpoint driver storage tables and columns, including table list, metadata, and task identity bindings.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM <checkpoint_schema>.<checkpoint_table> [WHERE task_id = <id>]

nodes.name: Cluster Version Inspection
nodes.content: List each TiDB, PD, and TiKV instance with its release version and git hash to separate a vulnerable release from a fixed one before and after an upgrade.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT type, instance, version, git_hash FROM information_schema.cluster_info;

nodes.name: Cluster Identity Log Extraction
nodes.content: Recover the original cluster ID and the maximum allocated ID from PD, TiDB, or TiKV logs of the last PD leader (grep "init cluster id" / "connect to PD cluster" / "idAllocator allocates a new id").

nodes.name: Cluster Log Table Search
nodes.content: Query information_schema.cluster_log across all instances for warning messages such as expensive_query within the abnormal time range to catch oversized statements not yet finished or below slow-log thresholds.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM information_schema.cluster_log WHERE time >= '<t_start>' AND time < '<t_end>' AND level = 'warn' AND message LIKE '%expensive_query%'

nodes.name: Cluster Processlist
nodes.content: Query information_schema.cluster_processlist to see statements currently running on all TiDB instances, their session ids, durations, and sql digests for live triage or killing a runaway session.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM information_schema.cluster_processlist;

nodes.name: Cluster Slow Query Table Diff
nodes.content: Aggregate information_schema.cluster_slow_query per digest inside the abnormal window and subtract digests already present in the baseline window to isolate newly slow statements.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT digest, count(*), sum(query_time) FROM information_schema.cluster_slow_query WHERE time >= '<t2_start>' AND time < '<t2_end>' AND Is_internal = false GROUP BY digest

nodes.name: Cluster task status SQL
nodes.content: SQL gate checks before maintenance: ADMIN SHOW DDL for ongoing DDL jobs, ADMIN CANCEL DDL JOB to cancel one, SHOW BACKUPS / SHOW RESTORES for running BR tasks, and SELECT * FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.CLUSTER_INFO for component versions.

attributes.sql_template: ADMIN SHOW DDL JOBS; ADMIN CANCEL DDL JOBS <job_id>; SHOW BACKUPS; SHOW RESTORES; SELECT * FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.CLUSTER_INFO;
SHOW CREATE TABLE t; SHOW INDEX FROM t; SELECT TIDB_PK_TYPE FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema=? AND table_name=?;

nodes.name: Component Log Read
nodes.content: Read TiDB component logs (TiDB/TiKV/PD/TiCDC) for error stacks and state transitions, e.g. search 'error on running processor' or FATAL entries around the failure time. Component logs exist as files only when --log-file was set at startup (otherwise stderr), and files are archived daily, so log searches must cover rotated files.

nodes.name: Conflict records SQL
nodes.content: Inspect the downstream conflict_records table populated by ignore-strategy imports to count and sample tolerated duplicate-key rows before deciding to re-import.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM <lightning_schema>.conflict_records LIMIT 100;

nodes.name: Continuous Profiling Access
nodes.content: Open the Dashboard Continuous Profiling page (via PD port) to enable collection and read FlameGraph/DAG profiles for any instance and time window.

nodes.name: ADMIN DDL Jobs SQL
nodes.content: Inspect and manage DDL jobs: ADMIN SHOW DDL JOBS (state, owner, progress), ADMIN CANCEL DDL JOBS to cancel queued jobs, and ADMIN PAUSE / RESUME DDL JOBS (GA v7.5.0) to temporarily stop resource-heavy jobs like index creation and resume them without restart.

attributes.sql_template: ADMIN SHOW DDL JOBS; ADMIN CANCEL DDL JOBS 'job_id'

nodes.name: DDL Job Inspection
nodes.content: Use ADMIN SHOW DDL JOBS and related DDL job queries to check the state, progress, and node running backend tasks such as ADD INDEX or IMPORT INTO.

attributes.sql_template: ADMIN SHOW DDL JOBS;

nodes.name: DEADLOCKS Table
nodes.content: Query information_schema.deadlocks to inspect recent deadlock chains (waiting and holding transactions); retryable deadlocks are collected only when deadlock-history-collect-retryable is enabled.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM information_schema.deadlocks;

nodes.name: PingCAP Clinic / Diag Collection
nodes.content: Diag collects a complete cluster diagnostic bundle in one step: logs and configs via SCP, kernel/system info via SSH, real-time config and performance sampling plus Prometheus alerts and metrics via component HTTP interfaces, and system variables via SQL; collection supports time-window selection (e.g. -f=-4h -t=-2h) with a size estimate before confirming. It also runs a quick local configuration health check (tiup diag collect --include=config, then tiup diag check) producing rule-based findings with knowledge-base links, and uploads bundles to Clinic Server for remote troubleshooting (direct upload, or encrypt-and-pack .diag for air-gapped networks, <=3GB compressed); only TiUP/Operator clusters v4.0+ are supported, upload requires an access token and region setting, uploads are resumable and retained up to 180 days.

args.command: diag collect / diag upload / diag check (tiup diag)

nodes.name: tiup diag Collector
nodes.content: Collects bundled diagnostic data (monitoring metrics, component logs, configs, optionally db_vars/perf/debug) from a TiUP-deployed TiDB or DM cluster for a time window (tiup diag collect <cluster> -f -4h -t -2h), with bandwidth limiting and per-node or per-type filtering.

nodes.name: dmctl check-task
nodes.content: dmctl check-task runs prechecks on a task config (privileges, schema compatibility, auto-increment conflicts) before start-task to reduce runtime failure probability.

nodes.name: DM Checkpoint Inspection
nodes.content: Read and correct global and per-table syncer checkpoints (binlog_name, binlog_pos, binlog_gtid) stored in the downstream dm_meta database.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM dm_meta.<task>_syncer_checkpoint WHERE id = '<source-id>'; UPDATE dm_meta.<task>_syncer_checkpoint SET binlog_name='<file>', binlog_pos=<pos> WHERE id='<source-id>';

nodes.name: dmctl query-status
nodes.content: dmctl query-status (optionally -s source) reports per-source relay state — masterBinlog vs relayBinlog/GTID, relayCatchUpMaster, relay stage — plus subtask unit states and error RawCause; relayCatchUpMaster=false with a lagging relayBinlog points at relay throughput rather than sync-unit problems.

nodes.name: DM Task Control
nodes.content: DM tasks are created and managed through dmctl or the OpenAPI (POST /api/v1/tasks); the task body carries task_mode (all/full/incremental), shard_mode, on_duplicate policy, binlog_filter_rule per table, full_migrate_conf (import_mode physical/logical, checksum, disk_quota, export/import threads) and incr_migrate_conf (repl_threads, repl_batch), which determine both migration speed and conflict behavior. DM tasks are created and managed through dmctl or the OpenAPI (POST /api/v1/tasks; GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/tasks/{task-name} with with_status=true); PUT requires the task stopped in incremental sync and only updates some fields. The task body carries task_mode (all/full/incremental), shard_mode, on_duplicate policy, binlog_filter_rule per table, full_migrate_conf (import_mode physical/logical, checksum, disk_quota, export/import threads) and incr_migrate_conf (repl_threads, repl_batch). dmctl purge-relay -s <source> --filename <binlog> [--sub-dir] purges relay logs before the named binlog (default: everything before the current sub-directory) when relay disk usage grows.

nodes.name: Execute SQL Diagnostics
nodes.content: Run diagnostic or administrative SQL against TiDB (SHOW, EXPLAIN, ANALYZE, ADMIN statements, information_schema/metrics_schema queries) to inspect cluster state or apply operational changes.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM information_schema.MEMORY_USAGE; SELECT * FROM information_schema.CLUSTER_MEMORY_USAGE;

nodes.name: Expensive Query Log
nodes.content: TiDB marks queries running longer than tidb_expensive_query_time_threshold (or touching more than the legacy expensive-threshold rows including intermediate results) with the [EXPENSIVE_QUERY] prefix in the instance log; slow logs also embed execution plans when tidb_record_plan_in_slow_log is on, and the general log can be routed to its own file via general-log-file.

nodes.name: EXPLAIN Plan Inspection
nodes.content: Views are non-materialized: EXPLAIN prints the underlying tables and indexes (the view definition is merged during optimization), so a slow 'view query' is diagnosed exactly like its expanded statement; verify index visibility via SHOW INDEXES where the Visible column marks invisible indexes the optimizer will skip.

attributes.sql_template: EXPLAIN <sql>

nodes.name: EXPLAIN ANALYZE
nodes.content: Execute the statement with EXPLAIN ANALYZE or attach to a live connection with EXPLAIN FOR CONNECTION to capture actual per-operator timings, rows, and RPC counts.

attributes.sql_template: EXPLAIN ANALYZE <sql>

nodes.name: Expression Pushdown Blacklist SQL
nodes.content: Manage per-expression pushdown through the blacklist table plus an admin reload. Manage per-expression pushdown and optimizer-rule disabling through blacklist tables plus an admin reload: INSERT/DELETE on mysql.expr_pushdown_blacklist then ADMIN RELOAD expr_pushdown_blacklist, and mysql.opt_rule_blacklist with ADMIN RELOAD opt_rule_blacklist to disable logical optimization rules.

attributes.sql_template: INSERT INTO mysql.expr_pushdown_blacklist VALUES('<','tikv',''); ADMIN RELOAD expr_pushdown_blacklist; DELETE FROM mysql.expr_pushdown_blacklist WHERE name='>'; ADMIN RELOAD expr_pushdown_blacklist;

nodes.name: GC Safepoint Query
nodes.content: Inspect the current GC safe point and service safe points through pd-ctl or the metrics schema to confirm replication consumers stay ahead of GC.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM mysql.tidb WHERE VARIABLE_NAME LIKE 'tikv_gc%'

nodes.name: Privilege inspection SQL
nodes.content: SQL probes for authentication state: SHOW GRANTS FOR 'user'@'host', SELECT from mysql.user for account existence, host patterns and lock state, and FLUSH PRIVILEGES to force a cache reload after direct-table edits. SHOW GRANTS FOR user [USING role...] lists effective grants and role privileges (viewing another user requires SELECT on mysql), which verifies privilege anomalies before changing them.

attributes.sql_template: SHOW GRANTS FOR 'user'@'host'; SELECT user, host, account_locked FROM mysql.user; FLUSH PRIVILEGES;

nodes.name: Remote Heap Profiling
nodes.content: Since v7.5.0 TiDB Dashboard supports remote heap profiling for TiKV: flame graph and call graph of the heap profile can be captured from the browser without jeprof on the host, pinpointing which allocations drive OOM or sustained high memory. Dashboard instance profiling runs on-demand (default 30 s, runs in background, results downloadable per instance or raw); since v7.5.0 TiKV heap profiles render as flame/call graphs remotely without jeprof, and manual profiling is unavailable while continuous profiling is enabled. Dashboard instance profiling runs on-demand (default 30 s, background, downloadable raw results) and since v5.3 continuous profiling stores flame graphs automatically (TiUP >= 1.7.0, off by default); since v7.5 TiKV heap profiles render remotely without jeprof, pinpointing allocations behind OOM or sustained memory growth.

nodes.name: Component HTTP status interface
nodes.content: Each component exposes an HTTP status endpoint (TiDB default port 10080): /status returns JSON liveness with current connection count, version and git hash; /schema_storage/<db>/<table> returns table storage statistics, usable as a keepalive probe independent of SQL connectivity.

nodes.name: IMPORT Job Inspection SQL
nodes.content: Manage IMPORT INTO jobs: SHOW IMPORT JOB <id> (or SHOW IMPORT) for progress and status of DETACHED jobs, CANCEL IMPORT JOB <id> to stop a running import.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM mysql.tidb_import_jobs ORDER BY end_time DESC LIMIT 10;

nodes.name: Column Metadata Check
nodes.content: Check column type, nullability, and default via INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS after a schema repair.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT COLUMN_NAME, COLUMN_TYPE, IS_NULLABLE, COLUMN_DEFAULT FROM information_schema.columns WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = '<db>' AND TABLE_NAME = '<table>'

nodes.name: INSPECTION_RESULT Sweep
nodes.content: Trigger built-in diagnostics with SELECT * FROM information_schema.inspection_result; rules cover config consistency, version consistency, node load, critical errors, and metric threshold checks across tidb/pd/tikv instances.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM information_schema.inspection_result;

nodes.name: Instance Lifecycle SQL
nodes.content: SHUTDOWN stops only the TiDB instance the client is connected to, never the whole cluster (requires SHUTDOWN privilege, self-managed only) — a single TiDB disappearing after this statement is expected behavior, and restart/orchestration belongs to the deployment layer.

nodes.name: Kill Session SQL
nodes.content: Terminate runaway queries or sessions: locate instance and session id in information_schema.cluster_processlist, then KILL (Global Kill enabled) or KILL TIDB connected to the owning instance; cancel DDL via ADMIN CANCEL DDL JOBS.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM information_schema.cluster_processlist; KILL <session_id>; ADMIN SHOW DDL JOBS; ADMIN CANCEL DDL JOBS <job_id>

nodes.name: Lightning Checkpoint Control
nodes.content: Resolve unusable Lightning checkpoint states with tidb-lightning-ctl checkpoint-error-destroy / checkpoint-error-ignore / checkpoint-remove / checkpoint-dump.

nodes.name: Lightning Control
nodes.content: tidb-lightning reads S3/GCS sources with URI-embedded credentials: default chain, force-path-style+endpoint for MinIO-style stores, role-arn assumption, or access-key/secret (+session-token); backend=local additionally needs a fast sorted-kv-dir on local SSD for index/color KV sorting.

nodes.name: Lightning web interface
nodes.content: Server mode (lightning.server-mode + status-addr) serves a web UI at status-addr showing import progress per table, errors of the previous task, and pause/resume or queue control over import tasks.

nodes.name: Lock View Tables
nodes.content: Query information_schema DATA_LOCK_WAITS, TIDB_TRX/CLUSTER_TIDB_TRX, and DEADLOCKS views (with TIDB_DECODE_SQL_DIGESTS) to see pessimistic lock waits, blocking transactions with their normalized SQL, and deadlock cycles.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT l.key, trx.*, tidb_decode_sql_digests(trx.all_sql_digests) AS sqls FROM information_schema.data_lock_waits l JOIN information_schema.cluster_tidb_trx trx ON l.current_holding_trx_id = trx.id;

nodes.name: Component Log Search
nodes.content: Searches all component logs by time range, level, keyword (regex supported) and component to locate errors such as GC worker progress, panics, or TiFlash failures

nodes.name: Cluster Management Operations
nodes.content: Cluster-level operations such as PD scheduling, placement rules, and store limits via manage_cluster.

args.notes: Topology, configuration, and PD control-plane changes applied outside SQL.

nodes.name: Set instance config dynamically
nodes.content: manage_instance with a set_config-style action applies dynamic parameter changes (SET GLOBAL system variables persist to the cluster; SET CONFIG modifies a TiKV/TiDB/PD instance config online where the item is dynamic).

nodes.name: MDL View Inspection
nodes.content: Inspect metadata-lock waits: SELECT * FROM mysql.tidb_mdl_view shows blocked DDL job id, table, query, blocking SESSION ID, TxnStart, and SQL_DIGESTS.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM mysql.tidb_mdl_view

nodes.name: Metrics Relation Graph
nodes.content: Dashboard Cluster Diagnostics renders a parent-child graph of internal metric durations over a time range: each node shows total duration, self duration, share of total query duration, and avg/P99-P90-P80, letting you attribute latency (e.g. tidb_execute vs pd_start_tso_wait) without manual metric math.

nodes.name: METRICS_SCHEMA Queries
nodes.content: METRICS_SCHEMA tables expose Prometheus metrics as SQL (e.g. SELECT from metrics_schema.tidb_query_duration WHERE quantile=0.99 grouped by sql_type/instance); EXPLAIN on such a query reveals the generated PromQL and step, proving the mapping from SQL rows to time series.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM metrics_schema.query_duration WHERE time > NOW() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR;

nodes.name: PD placement-rule API
nodes.content: PD HTTP API inspects and edits placement rules: GET /pd/api/v1/config/rules/group/tiflash lists TiFlash replication rules, DELETE /pd/api/v1/config/rule/tiflash/<id> removes one; also the entry point for checking PD scheduling state.

nodes.name: pd-ctl Scheduling Inspection
nodes.content: PD command-line interface for inspecting and steering scheduling: scheduler show/describe/config (balance, hot-region, evict-leader), operator show/add/remove, region scan/topread/topwrite/check, store (delete/cancel-delete/remove-tombstone/label/weight/limit), member (delete/leader resign/transfer/leader_priority), service-gc-safepoint, and tso parsing. member delete must never be used to remove PD nodes in production - use scale-in procedures.

nodes.name: pd-ctl Hotspot Query
nodes.content: Inspect current and historical hotspots with pd-ctl hot read|write|store|history commands, optionally filtered by region, store, peer, and leader role.

nodes.name: PD Hot Region Scheduling Control
nodes.content: Tune PD scheduling (hot-region schedule limits, cache sensitivity, scatter-range-scheduler, manual split-region operators, merge limits) to redistribute or split hot Regions.

nodes.name: pd-recover Metadata Repair
nodes.content: Run pd-recover against the deployed PD endpoint with the original cluster ID and an -alloc-id larger than the historical maximum to restore allocation and TSO serviceability.

nodes.name: PD Replication Status API
nodes.content: Read the current replication mode state through the PD HTTP endpoint /pd/api/v1/replication_mode/status.

nodes.name: PD Rule Bundle Commands
nodes.content: Inspect and modify placement rule groups with pd-ctl config placement-rules rule-bundle get/set/load/save.

nodes.name: PD Scheduler Control
nodes.content: Add, remove, or pause PD schedulers such as evict-slow-store-scheduler or evict-leader-scheduler and inspect scheduling operators.

nodes.name: PD Service Safepoint Owner Inspection
nodes.content: List PD service GC safepoint owners, their TTL/expiration, and safe point values via the PD control plane to identify stale owners.

nodes.name: Placement Inspection
nodes.content: information_schema.placement_policies lists every policy with PRIMARY_REGION/REGIONS/CONSTRAINTS, per-role constraints (LEADER/FOLLOWER/LEARNER_CONSTRAINTS), SCHEDULE, FOLLOWERS and LEARNERS — cross-check it against SHOW PLACEMENT and store labels when replica placement looks wrong.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM information_schema.placement_policies;

nodes.name: Plan Cache Hit Verification
nodes.content: Check whether an execution reused a cached plan and inspect plan-cache related settings to confirm hit or miss. ADMIN FLUSH [SESSION|INSTANCE] PLAN_CACHE clears cached plans (session scope by default) and @@last_plan_from_cache confirms whether the last execution reused a cached plan, which validates cache-clearing and plan-regression experiments.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT @@last_plan_from_cache; SELECT @@tidb_enable_non_prepared_plan_cache; SELECT @@tidb_session_plan_cache_size;

nodes.name: PLAN REPLAYER CAPTURE
nodes.content: PLAN REPLAYER DUMP [WITH STATS AS OF TIMESTAMP t] EXPLAIN [ANALYZE] <sql> packages TiDB version, config, session variables, bindings, table schema, statistics, and the plan into a ZIP for offsite analysis; PLAN REPLAYER IMPORT restores it into another cluster. The ZIP is retained on the node for about one hour and never contains table data.

attributes.sql_template: PLAN REPLAYER CAPTURE 'sql_digest' 'plan_digest'; SELECT * FROM mysql.plan_replayer_task; SELECT * FROM mysql.plan_replayer_status;

nodes.name: Read Pipeline Component Log
nodes.content: Read tool component logs (tidb-lightning.log, DM-master/DM-worker logs, TiCDC logs) to grep progress markers ('progress' every 5 minutes, 'the whole procedure completed'), error codes, and retry/EOF storms.

nodes.name: Read Log
nodes.content: TiDB log files rotate by size (max-size, default 300 MB), age (max-days), and count (max-backups) and can be gzip compressed, so evidence may live in rotated archives; a hung network-attached log disk can block the process, and log.timeout forces a panic instead of a silent hang.

nodes.name: Bounded recover-mvcc Inspection and Execution
nodes.content: Version-pinned tikv-ctl recover-mvcc run read-only first, then executable, against one exact Region and its complete peer Store set, with identity re-checked between inspection and execution.

nodes.name: Region Leader Distribution Check
nodes.content: Inspect Region, peer, and leader distribution for a table to confirm hotspot concentration or verify pre-split/scatter results.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT p.STORE_ID, COUNT(s.REGION_ID) AS leader_count FROM information_schema.TIKV_REGION_STATUS s JOIN information_schema.TIKV_REGION_PEERS p ON s.REGION_ID=p.REGION_ID WHERE s.TABLE_NAME='<table>' AND p.is_leader=1 GROUP BY p.STORE_ID; SHOW TABLE <table> REGIONS;

nodes.name: Region and Lock Inspection
nodes.content: Inspect Region metadata, peer placement, and transaction/MVCC lock state via information_schema region views before and after a lock resolution.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM information_schema.tikv_region_status WHERE TABLE_NAME = '<table>'

nodes.name: Region Peer Placement Validation
nodes.content: For every target Region, count healthy voter peers, check learner state and current leader, and verify fault-domain labels and Store capacity via information_schema region/store views.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT rs.TABLE_NAME, rp.STORE_ID, rp.PEER_ID, rp.ROLE, ss.LABELS, ss.STATE FROM information_schema.tikv_region_peers rp JOIN information_schema.tikv_region_status rs ON rp.REGION_ID = rs.REGION_ID JOIN information_schema.tikv_store_status ss ON rp.STORE_ID = ss.STORE_ID WHERE rs.TABLE_NAME = '<db.table>';

nodes.name: Resource Group SQL
nodes.content: SQL surface for resource isolation: CALIBRATE RESOURCE to estimate capacity, CREATE/ALTER/DROP RESOURCE GROUP for quotas, ALTER USER ... RESOURCE GROUP / SET RESOURCE GROUP / RESOURCE_GROUP() hint for binding.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM mysql.request_unit_by_group LIMIT 5;

nodes.name: Runaway Query Control SQL
nodes.content: Stop or throttle a specific runaway statement: QUERY WATCH (v7.5.0+) terminates matching queries, or bind the statement to a MAX_EXECUTION_TIME hint via CREATE GLOBAL BINDING so it is killed at the threshold.

attributes.sql_template: QUERY WATCH ADD SQL TEXT EXACT TO '<sql>'; CREATE GLOBAL BINDING FOR <sql> USING SELECT /*+ MAX_EXECUTION_TIME(1) */ ...; DROP GLOBAL BINDING FOR <sql>

nodes.name: ANALYZE_STATUS Inspection
nodes.content: information_schema.analyze_status shows cluster-level statistics-collection tasks (durable across restarts since v6.1.0) with STATE, FAIL_REASON, PROGRESS, REMAINING_SECONDS and INSTANCE, and mysql.analyze_jobs retains 7 days of history — the first stop when auto-analyze seems missing, failing, or never finishing.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM information_schema.analyze_status;

nodes.name: Show Create Table Schema Check
nodes.content: Compare the live target table definition with a saved schema identity using SHOW CREATE TABLE.

attributes.sql_template: SHOW CREATE TABLE <db.table>

nodes.name: SHOW VARIABLES probe
nodes.content: SHOW VARIABLES reads system variables while SHOW CONFIG (self-managed only, filterable by type/instance/name) reads component configuration files - two different dimensions, so a value that looks wrong in one may be intentionally different in the other.

attributes.sql_template: SHOW VARIABLES LIKE '<variable_name>';

nodes.name: SHOW WARNINGS
nodes.content: Show warnings or notes (e.g. warning 1815 inapplicable hints, bindSQL usage notes) generated by the last EXPLAIN or DML to reveal why the optimizer ignored a hint or which binding applied. Since v8.0 SHOW WARNINGS names the operator blocking Apply concurrency and reports why a PREPARE statement missed the plan cache, making it the first check for unexpected serial execution or cache misses.

attributes.sql_template: SHOW WARNINGS;

nodes.name: Slow Queries Inspection
nodes.content: Queries statements running longer than the slow-log threshold (300 ms by default) from the slow query log/system tables, with plan, coprocessor, wait and memory fields per query

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM information_schema.cluster_slow_query ORDER BY Query_time DESC LIMIT 20;

nodes.name: Slow Query Log
nodes.content: Read per-query stage timings (Query_time, Wait_TS, Cop_process, Cop_wait, Rewrite_time, Disk_max, Total/Processed_keys) from the slow query log to locate the slow stage of a statement. Slow log rows carry Prev_stmt for the statement preceding a COMMIT and use Index_names rather than numeric index ids; the pessimistic transaction mode is selected globally through tidb_txn_mode. Slow query log entries carry diagnosis-critical fields beyond latency: Backoff records 2PC commit-phase backoff details (lock waits, network retries), Prev_stmt shows the statement preceding a COMMIT, and Index_names replaces raw index ids for readability; slow logs feed both file inspection and INFORMATION_SCHEMA.CLUSTER_SLOW_QUERY.

nodes.name: SQL Binding (SPM)
nodes.content: Beyond CREATE GLOBAL BINDING, the Dashboard statement page offers fast plan binding (v6.6.0+): pick a plan and bind it in one click; it only supports simple SELECT/DELETE/UPDATE/INSERT/REPLACE without subqueries, TiFlash access, or joins of three or more tables, and requires the SUPER privilege, so permission errors there mean the session user lacks SUPER. Bindings are managed with CREATE [SESSION|GLOBAL] BINDING FOR ... USING ..., verified via SHOW [SESSION|GLOBAL] BINDINGS and EXPLAIN ANALYZE, and removed with DROP BINDING; ADMIN FLUSH BINDINGS persists them, ADMIN CAPTURE BINDINGS generates bindings for repeated statements, ADMIN EVOLVE BINDINGS triggers automatic evolution, and ADMIN RELOAD BINDINGS reloads the cache. Beyond CREATE GLOBAL BINDING, the Dashboard statement page offers fast plan binding (v6.6.0+): pick a plan and bind it in one click; it only supports simple SELECT/DELETE/UPDATE/INSERT/REPLACE without subqueries, TiFlash access, or joins of three or more tables, and requires the SUPER privilege.

attributes.sql_template: SHOW BINDINGS;

SELECT * FROM information_schema.inspection_result; SELECT * FROM information_schema.inspection_summary; SELECT * FROM information_schema.cluster_info; SELECT * FROM information_schema.cluster_config;

nodes.name: SQL Mode Inspection
nodes.content: Inspect or set the session/global sql_mode (e.g. ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY) with SQL to verify which semantic checks apply to aggregation queries.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT @@sql_mode;

nodes.name: TLS Status SQL
nodes.content: Inspect TLS cipher and certificate validity through status variables.

attributes.sql_template: SHOW SESSION STATUS LIKE 'Ssl_cipher_list'; SHOW GLOBAL STATUS LIKE 'Ssl_server_not_%';

nodes.name: Statement Summary Table
nodes.content: Dashboard statement and slow-query pages expose per-plan execution details: SQL samples, execution plans in table/text/graph form, and tabs for execution time, coprocessor reads, transactions, and slow-query context for the same plan digest.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM information_schema.cluster_statements_summary ORDER BY sum_latency DESC LIMIT <n>

nodes.name: Stats Dump HTTP Interface
nodes.content: Fetch table statistics JSON from the TiDB status port via /stats/dump/{db}/{table} and load it with LOAD STATS.

nodes.name: Statistics Health Check
nodes.content: Check per-table statistics health and refresh stale statistics so the optimizer re-estimates row counts.

attributes.sql_template: SHOW STATS_HEALTHY;

nodes.name: Store Label and Peer Inspection
nodes.content: Read current PD Store states, topology labels, and Region peer lists via the PD control plane to validate placement feasibility and recovery scope.

nodes.name: TiKV Store Status SQL
nodes.content: Query TiKV store state directly from SQL: SELECT STORE_ID, ADDRESS, STORE_STATE_NAME, CAPACITY, AVAILABLE, UPTIME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TIKV_STORE_STATUS to verify store health and free capacity.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT STORE_ID, ADDRESS, STORE_STATE, STORE_STATE_NAME, CAPACITY, AVAILABLE, UPTIME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TIKV_STORE_STATUS

nodes.name: sync-diff-inspector
nodes.content: Standalone data-consistency checker between upstream MySQL/TiDB and downstream TiDB; route rules map different schema/table names (schema-pattern, table-pattern, target-schema, target-table with wildcards) so replicated renamed tables can be verified. Standalone consistency checker: it chunks by TiDB statistics (run ANALYZE at low workload first), and collation mismatches (MySQL case-insensitive vs TiDB case-sensitive defaults) can produce false mismatches or unusable indexes — align collation or set index-fields explicitly; for renamed/sharded tables use route rules, and with a changed primary key set index-fields plus check-data-only. Generated repair SQL is reference-only and must be reviewed before execution, and avoid running checks at peak hours.

attributes.sql_template: sync-diff-inspector --config=diff.toml

nodes.name: Table Size Estimate
nodes.content: Estimate logical and on-disk table size by aggregating information_schema.TIKV_REGION_STATUS per region and dividing by METRICS_SCHEMA.store_size_amplification (cluster compression ratio).

attributes.sql_template: SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA, SUM(DATA_LENGTH), SUM(INDEX_LENGTH) FROM information_schema.tables GROUP BY TABLE_SCHEMA;

nodes.name: cdc cli / TiCDC OpenAPI
nodes.content: TiCDC is operated through cdc cli and the OpenAPI: DELETE /api/v2/changefeeds/{id} is idempotent and 200 only means the command was accepted; configuration updates must follow pause -> PUT (only target_ts, sink_uri, and complete replica_config are modifiable) -> resume, so an update attempt on a running changefeed fails or does not apply.

nodes.name: TiCDC Log Inspection
nodes.content: Read the raw TiCDC log to identify the failed event: DDL error text, table operation, and event commit timestamp (deduplicated).

nodes.name: tikv-ctl Diagnostics
nodes.content: tidb-ctl inspects TiDB-side state: etcd ddlinfo for current DDL information, putkey/delkey for /tidb/ddl/ keys, log to reformat one-line error stacks, and keyrange (--encode, --database, --table) to print global/table/index/row key ranges for TiKV-level debugging.

nodes.name: tidb-ctl Key Range Query
nodes.content: Compute the encoded key range of a database, table, or index with tidb-ctl keyrange --encode to scope placement rules to specific tables.

nodes.name: TiFlash replica SQL
nodes.content: SQL view and control of TiFlash replicas: SELECT from information_schema.tiflash_replica to list per-table replica counts, and ALTER TABLE ... SET TIFLASH REPLICA n to shrink replicas before scale-in. Set or shrink the TiFlash columnar replica of a table and inspect replication progress through information_schema.tiflash_replica; replica count must not exceed the TiFlash node count.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM information_schema.tiflash_replica WHERE REPLICA_COUNT > 1; ALTER TABLE db.t SET TIFLASH REPLICA 0;

args.ddl: ALTER TABLE t SET TIFLASH REPLICA n

nodes.name: tikv-ctl
nodes.content: tikv-ctl diagnoses and repairs TiKV: bad-regions lists corrupt-raft regions, consistency-check forces a region check, compact/compact-cluster manually compact kv/raft column families (with --bottommost, --threads) to reclaim space after deletes, diff compares region keys across DBs, and --log inspects logs; run version-matched via tiup ctl:v<version> tikv.

nodes.name: tikv-ctl Region Diagnostics
nodes.content: List bad regions, dump region properties (raft last/commit/apply index), run consistency-check, or tombstone a peer with tikv-ctl in local or remote mode. The tikv-ctl raft subcommand inspects the Raft state machine of specific Regions: raft region -r <id> (or --start/--end key ranges in Hex) prints RegionLocalState, RaftLocalState (term/vote/commit, last_index) and RegionApplyState (applied_index, truncated_state) to locate stuck applies or missing log entries during unavailability triage.

nodes.name: tiup cluster lifecycle
nodes.content: tiup status lists every launched instance with Name, Component, PID, Status (RUNNING or TERM), created time, directory, binary, and args, giving a quick per-instance liveness check outside the cluster tooling. tiup status lists every launched instance with Name, Component, PID, Status (RUNNING or TERM), created time, directory, binary, and args. tiup cluster patch replaces a component package for hotfixes (-R role or -N node scoped, --overwrite keeps it for future scale-out, --transfer-timeout bounds PD/TiKV leader transfer during restart, default 600s) and is also how Grafana and Alertmanager are upgraded; tiup cluster audit lists executed operations by audit-id for postmortems; tiup cluster exec runs commands on cluster hosts; tiup clean [tag|--all] kills and discards component instances.

nodes.name: Top SQL
nodes.content: Top SQL attributes CPU consumption to SQL digests and depends on the NgMonitoring component built into v5.4+ clusters; a 'required component NgMonitoring is not started' error means TiUP is older than v1.9.0 or monitoring_servers lacks ng_port (12020) with a Prometheus reload, and an 'unknown field' error on the Slow Queries page after upgrade is stale browser local storage (fixed since v5.0.3/v4.0.14).

nodes.name: Top SQL Attribution
nodes.content: Attribute CPU/resource consumption to specific statements and users over time to find which SQL class drives database time.

nodes.name: Transaction inspection SQL
nodes.content: SQL views of in-flight transactions: SELECT from information_schema.cluster_tidb_trx for cluster-wide active transactions with start time, and SHOW PROCESSLIST for per-session current statement duration.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT * FROM information_schema.cluster_tidb_trx; SHOW PROCESSLIST;

nodes.name: Trigger Inspection
nodes.content: Enumerate downstream table triggers with event and body to find table-bound work consuming sink write capacity.

attributes.sql_template: SELECT TRIGGER_NAME, EVENT_MANIPULATION, EVENT_OBJECT_TABLE, ACTION_STATEMENT FROM information_schema.triggers

nodes.name: Current TSO Position Capture
nodes.content: Capture the cluster current TSO inside a transaction to compare replicated position against the target recovery point.

attributes.sql_template: BEGIN; SELECT TIDB_CURRENT_TSO(); ROLLBACK;

nodes.name: TTL inspection SQL
nodes.content: SQL probes for TTL state: SHOW CREATE TABLE for TTL/TTL_ENABLE/TTL_JOB_INTERVAL attributes, SELECT from mysql.tidb_ttl_job_history for job timing, and SHOW VARIABLES for tidb_ttl_job_enable and schedule-window variables.

attributes.sql_template: SHOW CREATE TABLE t1; SELECT * FROM mysql.tidb_ttl_job_history ORDER BY created_time DESC LIMIT 20; SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'tidb_ttl%';

nodes.name: Unsafe Recovery Status View
nodes.content: View the current or historical Online Unsafe Recovery task state and progress stages with pd-ctl unsafe remove-failed-stores show.

nodes.name: Write Read-back Probe
nodes.content: Bounded surviving-endpoint write and read-back probe to prove the promoted endpoint admits writes.

attributes.sql_template: INSERT INTO <canary_table> ...; SELECT ... FROM <canary_table> WHERE id = <marker>;

nodes.name: Accidental Table Drop or Truncate
nodes.content: A table was dropped or truncated by mistake and must be recovered before its data is reclaimed by GC.

nodes.name: Account Auto Lockout
nodes.content: A user account is temporarily locked after repeated failed login attempts, or a password change is rejected with ERROR 1819 by the password complexity policy.

nodes.name: Admin Access Locked Out
nodes.content: The TiDB root password is lost or changed by mistake and no SQL account can administer the cluster.

nodes.name: Auto-Increment ID Conflict
nodes.content: When a table switches from explicit ID inserts to implicit allocation (for example after a migration cutover), cached auto-increment ranges on TiDB nodes can hand out IDs that collide with explicitly inserted rows, producing duplicate-key errors.

nodes.name: AUTO_RANDOM Explicit Insert Error
nodes.content: Inserts specifying the AUTO_RANDOM primary-key column fail with ERROR 8216 because explicit insertion on the auto_random column is disabled.

nodes.name: Backup or Restore Storage Access Failure
nodes.content: BR backup or restore fails to read/write the external storage (S3, GCS, Azure Blob, NFS) with permission or URI errors, stalling the job at startup or mid-run.

nodes.name: Backup Storage Access Failure
nodes.content: BR or TiKV cannot read or write the external backup storage (S3, GCS, Azure Blob), failing backup or restore with access-denied or credential errors.

nodes.name: Backup Throughput Low
nodes.content: BR backup tasks run far slower than expected on clusters under heavy workload because backup auto-tune deliberately limits backup CPU and I/O (default threads capped, 50% of CPU up to 8 threads since v5.4.0).

nodes.name: Backup Workload Interference
nodes.content: BR snapshot or log backup tasks running inside TiKV consume CPU and disk I/O during backup windows and compete with foreground traffic

nodes.name: Binding Not Used
nodes.content: A created plan binding does not affect the statement: last_plan_from_binding stays 0 or the plan still ignores the bound index.

nodes.name: TiDB Binlog Pipeline Failure
nodes.content: The Pump/Drainer binlog replication chain breaks - a Pump crash or critical binlog-write error stops Drainer replication, and downstream data diverges or lags behind the upstream.

nodes.name: Binlog Pump Unavailable
nodes.content: With binlog enabled, TiDB fetches registered Pump addresses from PD and streams binlog to all of them; if no Pump is registered TiDB refuses to start or blocks startup, and at least one Pump must stay online at runtime or binlog writes fail.

nodes.name: Binlog Replication Inconsistency
nodes.content: Drainer fails to replicate or the downstream drifts when upstream and downstream sql_mode differ, a replicated DDL is incompatible with the downstream engine, or a rename DDL touches filtered schemas; applied progress is tracked by the commit-ts checkpoint.

nodes.name: Binlog Replication Loop
nodes.content: Bidirectionally replicated clusters echo each other's transactions so rows multiply or diverge because loopback marking, channel IDs, or DDL direction are misconfigured.

nodes.name: Stale Pump/Drainer Node State
nodes.content: Pump/Drainer node state is self-maintained and reported to PD, so an abnormal exit (kill -9, panic, crash) leaves the node marked online in PD; after a full cluster restart a Pump may refuse to start because it cannot contact a Drainer PD still believes is online.

nodes.name: Binlog Write Failure
nodes.content: With binlog enabled, a Pump write failure either stops the whole TiDB service (ignore-error false, default) or silently stops binlog writing and only bumps tidb_server_critical_error_total (ignore-error true).

nodes.name: BR Restore Decryption Failure
nodes.content: Restoring an encrypted snapshot fails or the data cannot be read because the supplied crypter method or key does not match the encryption parameters used at backup time.

nodes.name: BR Restore Interrupted
nodes.content: A snapshot or log restore aborts mid-run on recoverable errors such as disk exhaustion or node crash, leaving the cluster partially restored.

nodes.name: CDC Downstream Data Redundancy
nodes.content: Downstream tables replicated by TiCDC accumulate duplicate rows because source tables lack a valid index and INSERT/REPLACE events are replayed at least once.

nodes.name: CDC Kafka Consumer Disorder
nodes.content: Kafka consumers of TiCDC streams observe out-of-order or inconsistent data when rows are spread across partitions by the ts dispatcher or when the configured index/columns dispatcher cannot be applied.

nodes.name: CDC Checkpoint Lag
nodes.content: A changefeed checkpoint falls behind the write workload when incremental scan is rate limited, sink or old-value memory quotas cap throughput, or downstream sinks stall.

nodes.name: CDC Pulsar Sink Failure
nodes.content: A TiCDC changefeed writing to Pulsar fails or stalls on protocol, authentication, TLS, producer-cache, or timeout misconfiguration.

nodes.name: Certificate Login Denied
nodes.content: A user configured with REQUIRE ISSUER/SUBJECT/SAN/CIPHER gets ERROR 1045 access denied because the presented client certificate does not satisfy one of the required attributes or SSL is not in use.

nodes.name: Changefeed Interrupted or Lagging
nodes.content: A TiCDC changefeed's checkpoint falls behind the upstream TSO or stops advancing: sink throughput drops, latency spikes after pause/resume, or replication stalls after BR/Lightning restore on replicated tables. Replication lag of a changefeed grows beyond its normal watermark; documented alerting threshold is 600 seconds.

nodes.name: Cloud Live Migration Jitter
nodes.content: Cloud VM live-migration maintenance events briefly degrade VM performance, causing intermittent query latency spikes on affected TiDB, TiKV, or PD nodes without any cluster configuration change.

nodes.name: Cluster Space Low
nodes.content: Cluster storage usage exceeds about 80% of capacity or stores report low space, which stops PD from placing new replicas and can halt writes

nodes.name: Clustered Index Data Inconsistency
nodes.content: An INSERT ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE on a table whose clustered primary key contains an ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP column can change the row handle without marking it changed, leaving secondary index entries inconsistent with the clustered record and surfacing ERROR 8134/8141.

nodes.name: Component RPC Timeout
nodes.content: Requests fail with ERROR 9001 PD server timeout, ERROR 9002 TiKV server timeout, or ERROR 9012 TiFlash timeout, pointing at component health, load, or network between TiDB and the component.

nodes.name: Component TLS Handshake Failure
nodes.content: TiDB, TiKV, PD, TiFlash, or TiCDC cannot authenticate each other after TLS enablement, or control tools cannot reach HTTPS endpoints without client certificates.

nodes.name: Config Change Not Effective
nodes.content: An operator modifies a component configuration file but runtime behavior does not change; typical root causes are configs not being loaded (TiKV needs --config at start, PD reads its file only on first bootstrap and afterwards is changed via pd-ctl) or monitor/cluster clock skew hiding new metrics.

nodes.name: Connection Lost
nodes.content: Clients get ERROR 2013 Lost connection during query or connections drop unexpectedly; TiDB logs EOF when it discovers the disconnect on write-back.

nodes.name: Connection Exhaustion
nodes.content: TiDB rejects new client connections once the instance connection limit (instance.max_connections or max-server-connections, default unlimited) is reached, typically after pool leaks or traffic spikes.

nodes.name: Dashboard Console Inaccessible
nodes.content: TiDB Dashboard pages return errors, blank content, or broken static resources, typically after topology, proxy, or path changes.

nodes.name: Dashboard Login Denied
nodes.content: A user cannot sign in to TiDB Dashboard because the SQL account lacks required privileges such as PROCESS, SHOW DATABASES, CONFIG, or DASHBOARD_CLIENT.

nodes.name: Dashboard Unreachable Or Redirected
nodes.content: The TiDB Dashboard UI is unreachable, redirects to an internal address, or cannot be opened via a second network interface.

nodes.name: Data Index Inconsistency
nodes.content: Data in TiDB diverges from its source or from expected invariants, such as missing rows, divergent values, or broken unique constraints after replication or repair.

nodes.name: Datetime Value Overflow or Misparse
nodes.content: Date and time values convert incorrectly or become zero because they exceed type ranges, or two-digit years are misinterpreted under century rules.

nodes.name: DDL Backfill Load Impact
nodes.content: Physical DDL such as ADD INDEX backfills rows in the background reorg phase, adding read/write pressure that can degrade application response time while the DDL keeps running even if the issuing TiDB restarts.

nodes.name: DDL Backfill Resource Pressure
nodes.content: Index backfill and DDL reorg write batches to TiKV concurrently with business traffic, causing write latency and QPS degradation; a DDL job is canceled after its retry count passes tidb_ddl_error_count_limit (default 512).

nodes.name: DDL Issue
nodes.content: DDL statements take far longer than expected, queue behind each other, hang indefinitely, or are cancelled, often disturbing concurrent DML.

nodes.name: DDL Limit Violation
nodes.content: CREATE/ALTER statements fail with limit errors such as index key length too long, too many columns, or too many indexes on a table.

nodes.name: DDL Slow or Stuck
nodes.content: DDL statements take far longer than expected or appear queued: DDLs run serially cluster-wide, and after abnormal shutdowns each DDL state change can wait 2 * lease when TiDB cannot reach PD or registration data was not cleaned.

nodes.name: Transaction Deadlock Errors
nodes.content: Two or more pessimistic transactions wait on each other's held locks (or lock in inconsistent order), forming a lock-wait cycle that TiDB breaks by rolling back one transaction with ERROR 1213.

nodes.name: Component Fails To Start After Deployment
nodes.content: A newly deployed or restarted component never enters running state, typically due to missing runtime prerequisites such as JRE 8 for TiSpark or inaccessible config-referenced resources.

nodes.name: High Disk I/O
nodes.content: Node-exporter alert NODE_disk_write_latency_more_than_16ms fires when average disk write latency (rate of write time over writes completed) exceeds 16 ms; investigate the Disk Performance / Disk Latency / Disk I/O Utilization panels.

nodes.name: Disk Read-Only
nodes.content: A filesystem turns read-only or inodes run out, so the component on that host can no longer write data or logs

nodes.name: TiKV Disk Space Exhaustion
nodes.content: A TiKV store runs out of disk ('IO error: No space left on device While appending to file'), and PD also stops migrating regions onto stores with less than 20% free capacity.

nodes.name: Space Not Reclaimed After Delete
nodes.content: After DELETE/TRUNCATE/DROP, TiKV disk usage stays high: TRUNCATE/DROP free space only after GC (default life time about 10 minutes), while DELETE rows are reused only when RocksDB compaction rewrites the data, and leftover empty keys drag query speed until Region Merge.

nodes.name: DM Duplicate Entry Error
nodes.content: Merging sharded tables fails with ERROR 1062 (23000) Duplicate entry for key 'PRIMARY' because per-shard auto-increment primary keys overlap across shards.

nodes.name: DM Oversized Binlog Event
nodes.content: An upstream binlog file larger than 4 GB overflows the uint32 binlog position, breaking DM relay pulling or incremental replication with event-diff, ERROR 1236, or checksum-mismatch errors.

nodes.name: DM Replication Resume Anomaly
nodes.content: After a DM worker restart or network break, binlog events between checkpoint and safemode_exit_point may replay downstream, so DM re-enables safe mode (default 60 seconds, two checkpoint intervals) to make repeats idempotent.

nodes.name: DM Replication Interrupted
nodes.content: A DM incremental or full migration task is interrupted by upstream connection loss, a DM restart, or a GTID/checkpoint breakage, leaving replication stale or reporting binlog errors.

nodes.name: DM Replication Stall
nodes.content: A DM migration/replication task stops making progress: query-status reports paused sync units, unresolvedGroups or blockingDDLs, and downstream data lags the upstream shards.

nodes.name: DM Shard DDL Conflict
nodes.content: Optimistic-mode shard DDL creates upstream/downstream schema or data inconsistency that DM reports but does not repair, or a pessimistic shard DDL lock stays unsynced forever because a source was removed mid-DDL.

nodes.name: DM Task Paused
nodes.content: A DM subtask stays Paused over 20 minutes, a sharding DDL stays pending or errors, or DM-master/DM-worker health alerts fire

nodes.name: DM TLS Handshake Failure
nodes.content: dmctl or DM components cannot establish TLS connections to each other or to upstream/downstream databases, reporting certificate, CN, or handshake errors.

nodes.name: DR Auto-Sync State Degraded
nodes.content: PD replication mode leaves sync into async or sync-recover, or the Region replica contract fails to converge after a role exchange despite the control-plane request succeeding.

nodes.name: DR Replication State Change
nodes.content: PD replication state leaves sync (async or sync-recover) in a DR Auto-Sync deployment, enlarging the disaster data-loss window

nodes.name: Drainer Checkpoint and GC Gap
nodes.content: Drainer cannot resolve table schemas or resume because the checkpoint TS fell behind the GC safe point, or multiple Drainer nodes overwrite each other's replication progress.

nodes.name: Background Task Interference on OLTP Nodes
nodes.content: The DXF schedules distributed internal tasks across TiDB nodes; when nodes dedicated via tidb_service_scope are missing or down, background tasks fall back to empty-scope nodes and contend with foreground application traffic.

nodes.name: Encryption At Rest Key Problem
nodes.content: TiKV cannot decrypt data files because the master key for encryption at rest is missing, rotated incorrectly, or incompatible, blocking store startup.

nodes.name: Export Tool Failure or Slow Export
nodes.content: Dumpling or other export tooling fails or crawls: local disk space insufficient, upstream memory exhausted, or floods of retries and EOF errors in component logs.

nodes.name: Failover Fencing Gap
nodes.content: An old SQL writer is not provably fenced before a DR failover promotes the surviving side, risking a second concurrent writer and split-brain writes.

nodes.name: Full Table Scan
nodes.content: Queries scan the whole table (TableFullScan/IndexFullScan) or read vastly more rows than needed because no usable index matches the predicates.

nodes.name: GC Backlog and Space Bloat
