nodes.content: GC falls behind safe-point forwarding or retains too many MVCC versions, so disk usage keeps growing and range scans slow down even without new data.

nodes.name: GC Not Running
nodes.content: No successful GC task on a TiKV instance for 24 hours, so MVCC versions keep accumulating and queries slow down over time

nodes.name: Global Sort Backend Task OOM
nodes.content: ADD INDEX or IMPORT INTO tasks that use the DXF Global Sort operator consume large TiDB CPU and memory, causing TiDB OOM or business-query interference when run on undersized or shared nodes.

nodes.name: High Database Time
nodes.content: The cluster-wide database time (total SQL service time) saturates relative to capacity, showing up as high CPU, rising latency, and queuing across the workload.

nodes.name: Hint Ineffective
nodes.content: Optimizer hints silently fail to change the plan or ERROR 1815 'Can't find a proper physical plan' appears after adding hints.

nodes.name: Idle Sessions Terminated
nodes.content: User sessions disappear without application errors being the cause: sessions inside a transaction that stay idle longer than tidb_idle_transaction_timeout are killed by TiDB.

nodes.name: Import Conflict Errors
nodes.content: Duplicate primary/unique keys during import either terminate the task (strategy error/empty), overwrite or ignore rows (replace/ignore with a tolerant conflict.threshold), or silently diverge when detection is off - later caught by the checksum step or by row counts not matching unique-index counts.

nodes.name: Import Disk Blowout
nodes.content: Physical (local backend) import fills the local disk with encoded and sorted temporary files; on write failure TiDB Lightning exits, so imports stall or abort when disk-quota and sorted-kv-dir are not sized.

nodes.name: Import Conflict and Type Errors
nodes.content: Imports stop or silently skip rows when source data hits type errors or primary/unique key conflicts, governed by lightning.max-error (default 0) and conflict.threshold (default 10000) with strategies error or replace.

nodes.name: Interrupted Import / Stale Checkpoint
nodes.content: An import that dies mid-task leaves checkpoints, sorted-kv temporary data, and lightning_metadata behind; resuming against changed source files or schemas imports wrong data, and leftover metadata corrupts later imports.

nodes.name: Import Job Stall
nodes.content: A Lightning or IMPORT INTO job stalls or crawls in a phase such as open-engine, ingest, or checksum, blocking data availability

nodes.name: Import Interferes With Online Load
nodes.content: Physical import saturates TiKV writes and pauses scheduling for target-table Regions, so online workloads see TPM drops and P99 latency increases - the damage is largest for low-concurrency latency-sensitive applications.

nodes.name: Import Precheck Refusal
nodes.content: TiDB Lightning prechecks abort the import before it starts: unreachable or too-old cluster, missing storage permissions, insufficient disk (index-inflated estimates), too many empty Regions (more than max(1000, 3x tables)), oversized unsliced CSVs, changed sources under breakpoint recovery, non-empty target tables, or running PITR/changefeed in physical import mode.

nodes.name: Import vs CDC/Log-Backup Incompatibility
nodes.content: Physical import (Lightning or IMPORT INTO) fails its compatibility check while PITR or a changefeed runs; bypassing it means imported rows never enter log backup and TiCDC cannot keep up with import speed, so replication lag grows.

nodes.name: Incremental Restore Write Conflict
nodes.content: An incremental restore is applied before its base full restore completes, or writes continue on the target cluster during restore, causing write conflicts on the restored keys.

nodes.name: Index Data Inconsistency
nodes.content: Table data and index diverge (typically after replica loss): SELECT fails with 'inconsistent index ... handle count N isn't equal to value count M' and ADMIN CHECK INDEX reports mismatched entries, including dangling index keys.

nodes.name: Hash Join Probe Side Over-Scan
nodes.content: A hash-join query scans far more rows on the probe side than the build-side cardinality justifies, wasting I/O and CPU on rows that cannot match the hash table.

nodes.name: JWT Token Auth Failure
nodes.content: Users authenticating with tidb_auth_token are rejected because JWT claims (sub, iss, iat, exp, email) do not match the user definition, the token is expired, JWKS is stale, or TLS with mysql_clear_password is not in place.

nodes.name: TiKV Background Storage Error
nodes.content: RocksDB background SST corruption lets TiKV keep writing but error on reads of damaged ranges while PD schedules the damaged peers away; TiKV panics if recovery does not finish within background-error-recovery-window (default 1h).

nodes.name: TiKV Busy
nodes.content: TiDB reports ERROR 9003 TiKV Server is Busy when the TiKV write path is overloaded and back-pressures requests, usually under workload spikes or write stalls.

nodes.name: Transaction Too Large
nodes.content: Bulk writes fail with 'transaction too large' or commit extremely slowly: entries are limited to 6 MB (txn-entry-size-limit, up to 120 MB) and transactions to 100 MB total (txn-total-size-limit, up to 10 GB), and oversized transactions risk conflicts and expensive rollbacks.

nodes.name: Lazy Uniqueness Check Failure
nodes.content: With tidb_constraint_check_in_place_pessimistic=OFF, unique constraint checks are deferred until commit or later lock, so transactions can fail at COMMIT or at a later DML with Duplicate entry (1062), Write conflict (9007, reason=LazyUniquenessCheck), or 8147 LazyUniquenessCheckFailure.

nodes.name: Frequent Leader Drops
nodes.content: TiKV instances drop Region leaders frequently or re-elections spike, causing transient latency and error bursts.

nodes.name: Lightning Checkpoint Admission Failure
nodes.content: A resumable Lightning import fails admission or terminal acceptance when checkpoint generation, reservation, lease, or resume-gate evidence no longer matches the current task identity.

nodes.name: Lightning Source File Unmatched
nodes.content: TiDB Lightning finishes almost instantly without importing data because source file names do not match expected patterns, or the task errors on unsupported compression variants inside the data directory.

nodes.name: Lightning Import Capacity Shortfall
nodes.content: Lightning physical import fails or is refused because Store free space cannot hold encoded key-values, indexes, sort or temporary data, replication, and compaction headroom.

nodes.name: Lightning Import Failure
nodes.content: A TiDB Lightning import terminates abnormally or never reaches completion: the log lacks the 'the whole procedure completed' marker (note that the final 'tidb lightning exit' line only means the process exited, not success), or the import progress stops advancing.

nodes.name: Lightning Import Fault
nodes.content: TiDB Lightning imports run far slower than expected, abort unexpectedly (SIGHUP, Context canceled), or report errors such as checksum mismatch, invalid checkpoint status, entry too large, or invalid time format.

nodes.name: Lightning Import Slow
nodes.content: Lightning import throughput is far below expectations: progress increments slowly, worker concurrency is underused, or the sorted-key-value temp storage becomes the bottleneck.

nodes.name: Lock Contention
nodes.content: Multiple transactions contend for the same row or table locks, serializing execution and inflating latency or causing lock-wait timeouts.

nodes.name: Lock Wait and Deadlock Storms
nodes.content: Pessimistic transactions block on lock waits (TiKV per-lock timeout 1s, statement retry limit 256) and report lock wait timeouts or deadlocks under contended keys.

nodes.name: Log Backup Checkpoint Lag
nodes.content: Log backup checkpoint falls behind (RPO over 10 minutes warns, over 30 minutes is critical), the task pauses, fails, or its GC safe point is exceeded

nodes.name: Log Backup Task Error
nodes.content: A log backup task leaves NORMAL status (ERROR after network partition or checkpoint loss), or resume fails with ErrBackupGCSafepointExceeded because the checkpoint data was already garbage collected.

nodes.name: Long Running Transaction
nodes.content: A transaction staying open beyond the GC horizon holds back the GC safe point, letting MVCC versions and disk usage accumulate

nodes.name: Low Throughput Under High Concurrency
nodes.content: Aggregate QPS or throughput stays well below hardware capacity although client concurrency is high and instances look correctly configured.

nodes.name: Malformed Lock Blocking GC
nodes.content: A TiKV lock whose async-commit invariant min_commit_ts > start_ts is violated, or a Put lock without its default record, is treated as malformed; GC Resolve Locks cannot resolve it and the safepoint stalls while obsolete MVCC versions accumulate.

nodes.name: DDL Blocked by Metadata Lock
nodes.content: With metadata lock (default since v6.5.0) a DDL such as ADD INDEX or TRUNCATE waits indefinitely while long-running transactions that touched the table keep the old metadata, so the DDL appears stuck in queue.

nodes.name: Memory Limit and Spill
nodes.content: Queries or transactions exceed memory quotas: operators spill to disk or the query is killed by memory control, often caused by underestimated inputs feeding blocking operators or oversized write transactions cached in TiDB memory.

nodes.name: Metadata Lock Wait
nodes.content: DDL state changes stall waiting for old-schema transactions to finish, so DDL jobs queue and schema changes appear frozen

nodes.name: Incremental Migration GC Gap
nodes.content: An incremental replication task (TiCDC or DM) cannot start or fails because the required start timestamp has already been garbage-collected: history data was removed during a long full-migration or backup/restore window.

nodes.name: Mistaken Delete/Update
nodes.content: An application or operator ran a wrong DELETE/UPDATE (or dropped a table), and affected rows must be recovered before GC removes the old versions.

nodes.name: Monitoring Config Lost or Unreachable
nodes.content: Alert rules or Grafana dashboards revert to defaults after cluster operations, or Alertmanager/monitoring endpoints cannot be reached through a proxy.

nodes.name: MPP Mode Not Selected
nodes.content: Queries keep running on TiKV although TiFlash replicas exist because MPP is blocked by missing or still-replicating replicas, unsupported operators, or tidb_allow_mpp/enforce_mpp settings; EXPLAIN then emits a warning explaining the block.

nodes.name: Node CPU High
nodes.content: Host CPU usage exceeds about 80% or load per core exceeds 1 on a TiDB/TiKV/PD machine, degrading whatever component runs there

nodes.name: Slow Node Offline/Online
nodes.content: Taking a TiKV store offline (or bringing a new store online) takes far longer than expected: replicas/leaders drain slowly or the store stays in Offline state instead of reaching Tombstone.

nodes.name: Inter-Node Port Blocked
nodes.content: Firewall rules on target machines block cluster ports, breaking RPC, raft heartbeat and client traffic between nodes.

nodes.name: Node Resource Pressure
nodes.content: A host shows sustained resource pressure such as memory overcommit, swapping, or IO saturation that degrades the TiDB component it runs.

nodes.name: Online Unsafe Recovery Needed
nodes.content: TiKV Stores are permanently damaged or unrecoverable, leaving Regions without quorum and requiring a lossy PD-owned Online Unsafe Recovery rather than a normal Store drain.

nodes.name: Process OOM
nodes.content: A TiDB or TiKV process is OOM-killed or grows memory sharply: clients see lost connections, the process restarts, and system OOM-killer records appear.

nodes.name: Uneven Leader/Region Distribution
nodes.content: PD balancing fails to even out leaders or regions across TiKV stores: counts stay skewed or balance operators stall, often noticed as per-store load asymmetry or slow scaling.

nodes.name: PD Performance Bottleneck
nodes.content: PD cannot keep up with TSO allocation or Region heartbeats: TSO handle time rises and TiKV heartbeat pending items accumulate, adding latency to every transaction cluster-wide.

nodes.name: PD Leader Election and OOM
nodes.content: PD switches leader, fails or slows elections, or is OOM, causing TiDB SQL to time out on PD requests.

nodes.name: PD Metadata Loss Identity Mismatch
nodes.content: PD quorum loss or a rebuilt PD endpoint answers health probes while preserved TiKV members reject its new cluster identity, leaving the data plane unable to register with the control plane.

nodes.name: Slow PD Metadata and Routing
nodes.content: PD leader switching or Region routing updates take tens of seconds in clusters with a very large number of Regions.

nodes.name: PD Request Slow
nodes.content: PD request handling latency breaches its normal range (p99 completed commands above 5 ms), slowing every TSO and metadata round trip

nodes.name: PD Slow Disk Write
nodes.content: etcd WAL fsync on PD exceeds 1 second, risking PD leader timeout and TSO persistence failure that can halt the whole cluster

nodes.name: PD Startup Failure
nodes.content: PD fails to start or is unusable at startup with errors such as 'TiKV cluster is not bootstrapped', 'etcd cluster ID mismatch', or encryption master key file permission failures.

nodes.name: PD TSO Unavailability Jitter
nodes.content: PD leader switchover or network isolation interrupts timestamp allocation, causing short write latency spikes and QPS dips; exhausted local TSO caches on TiKV amplify the effect under bursty writes.

nodes.name: Suboptimal Plans After Restart
nodes.content: Queries perform poorly right after a TiDB node starts: statements executed before statistics finish loading may run with degraded plans.

nodes.name: Pessimistic Lock Errors
nodes.content: Pessimistic transactions fail with lock wait timeout (ERROR 1205), pessimistic lock retry limit reached, or TTL manager timeout after exceeding max-txn-ttl.

nodes.name: PITR Checkpoint Resume Failure
nodes.content: A BR checkpoint restore cannot be safely retried because checkpoint identity (upstream cluster, BackupTS, log start-ts, restored-ts, target identity) no longer matches the current request or the target changed after the failed attempt.

nodes.name: PITR Log Chain Gap
nodes.content: The requested PITR recovery point is unreachable because log backup data does not cover the interval from the usable snapshot boundary, or a global-checkpoint, retention-window, or object-inventory segment is missing, corrupt, or out of retention.

nodes.name: Placement Policy Unsatisfied
nodes.content: A placement policy DDL is accepted but the requested replica layout stays PENDING/INPROGRESS or unsatisfiable because healthy TiKV Stores and labels cannot provide the requested followers, fault domains, or constraints.

nodes.name: Placement Policy Violation
nodes.content: Replicas or Raft leaders sit outside the intended locations: a placement policy was not applied, was overridden by inheritance rules, or leader/replica counts do not match the configured PRIMARY_REGION/FOLLOWERS settings.

nodes.name: Plan Cache Miss
nodes.content: Prepared or non-prepared statements repeatedly recompile instead of reusing cached plans: compile time dominates database time and per-statement latency includes avoidable optimization overhead.

nodes.name: Plan Regression
nodes.content: A statement class switches to a slower plan (plan flip) after data growth, statistics change, or a version upgrade, despite the schema being unchanged.

nodes.name: Login or Privilege Change Not Effective
nodes.content: Access denied errors or privileges that behave inconsistently across TiDB nodes arise from host-pattern mismatches in accounts, GRANT auto-creation blocked by sql_mode, or privilege-cache propagation delays after network issues; direct edits to mysql.user can leave privilege state incomplete.

nodes.name: Client Connection Drops via Proxy or Restart
nodes.content: Client sessions are severed when TiDB servers are hard-restarted (non-rolling) or TiProxy itself restarts/upgrades; session migration additionally requires identical session-token-signing certs on all TiDB instances and a graceful-wait-before-shutdown longer than the longest transaction.

nodes.name: QPS Drop and Latency Spike
nodes.content: Throughput fluctuates periodically or irregularly while average capacity looks sufficient, typically from background task preemption or uneven resource sharing.

nodes.name: Query Latency High
nodes.content: TiDB request handling latency breaches its alert threshold (p99 above 1 second), indicating lock waits, plan regressions, saturation, or topology round trips

nodes.name: Raftstore Stuck
nodes.content: TiKV raftstore threads stall or channels fill (channel full, leader drops, raft log lag above thousands of entries), stalling writes on the node

nodes.name: Read Hotspot
nodes.content: Read requests concentrate on one Region or TiKV node (bright horizontal band in Key Visualizer, coprocessor CPU skewed to one store), so reads queue although the cluster has idle capacity.

nodes.name: Read Hotspot on Region Leaders
nodes.content: All reads of a hot Region concentrate on its leader and saturate one store while followers idle, capping read throughput regardless of total cluster capacity.

nodes.name: Region Disaster Switchover
nodes.content: A primary region fails and traffic must move to the surviving region, with replication lag or missing redo application threatening the recoverable point.

nodes.name: Region Scheduling Stall or Storm
nodes.content: Replica repair or rebalance stalls (a down store is not replenished before max-store-down-time of 30m, pending peers pile up) or scheduling storms saturate snapshot I/O and foreground traffic.

nodes.name: Region Unavailable
nodes.content: ERROR 9005 Region is unavailable: the accessed Region's Raft group cannot serve requests (insufficient replicas, leader loss, TiKV busy or down).

nodes.name: Region Replica Shortage
nodes.content: Regions whose replica count is below max-replicas exceed the alert threshold, meaning stores are down, draining, or labels leave no eligible target

nodes.name: Replicated Temporal DDL Time Zone Failure
nodes.content: A TIMESTAMP or temporal DDL accepted in an upstream session is rejected by the downstream MySQL-compatible session because the same literal maps outside the downstream type's valid range under different time-zone settings.

nodes.name: Resolved TS / Safe TS Stall
nodes.content: Long-lived or large in-flight transactions keep prewrite locks and pin resolved-ts via their start-ts, so stale reads lag and commits slow down; CheckLeader delays from network problems have the same effect.

nodes.name: Resource Group Throttled
nodes.content: A workload's queries slow down or stall while the cluster has spare capacity: its resource group exceeded its RU quota and is being throttled (resource control GA since v7.1.0).

nodes.name: Resource Group Throttling
nodes.content: Requests bound to a non-BURSTABLE resource group wait when cluster resources are exhausted and error out if the wait is too long; RU quota (RU_PER_SEC) and priority of the bound group directly cap tenant throughput.

nodes.name: Restore Table Creation Slow
nodes.content: A large-table-count restore spends most of its time creating schemas because serial execution changes the DDL schema version once per table instead of once per batch.

nodes.name: Resource Group Quota Errors
nodes.content: Requests fail with ERROR 8252 "Exceeded resource group quota limitation" when the estimated RU wait passes the Local Token Bucket maximum wait (default 30s) under concurrency spikes, large transactions, or big queries.

nodes.name: Runaway Query
nodes.content: A query exceeds execution-time or resource thresholds and is identified as runaway, degrading shared resources; detected via runaway identification, expensive query logs, or statements summary.

nodes.name: Information Schema Errors
nodes.content: DML fails with 'Information schema is changed' or 'Information schema is out of date' while concurrent DDL runs or TiDB cannot refresh schema in time.

keywords: Information schema is out of date

nodes.name: Sensitive Data Exposed in Logs
nodes.content: Log files or shared diagnostics contain plaintext literals from user SQL (credentials, personal data), violating data-handling policy during log collection and sharing.

nodes.name: TiProxy Session Migration Failure
nodes.content: Connections behind TiProxy fail to migrate between TiDB nodes because session-token signing certificate and key are missing or differ across TiDB nodes, or clients are disconnected on expired passwords.

nodes.name: Slow Bulk Delete
nodes.content: Large DELETE operations run progressively slower or fail, because single-statement bulk deletes hit transaction size limits and GC deletion flags slow later batches.

nodes.name: Unpruned Partition Scan
nodes.content: Queries on partitioned tables scan all or far too many partitions because pruning did not apply, showing many per-partition scan operators in the plan.

nodes.name: Slow Queries
nodes.content: SQL statements whose latency exceeds expectations; the entry symptom for plan, resource, and configuration mis-tuning. The instance slow-log threshold defaults to 300ms and feeds this trigger directly.

nodes.name: Slow or Failed TiKV Store
nodes.content: A TiKV store is unreachable beyond max-store-down-time or its slow-node score reaches the slow threshold, so leaders are evicted and replica rebalancing starts while latency accumulates on delayed requests.

nodes.name: Slow TiKV Node
nodes.content: PD marks a store as slow (Store Slow Score above 80 from raftstore inspection), usually a disk or raftstore bottleneck on one node

nodes.name: Backup Snapshot GC Conflict
nodes.content: Garbage collection advances the safe point past the timestamp a long-running reader needs, so snapshot reads, exports, or flashback operations fail with 'GC life time is shorter than transaction duration' style errors.

nodes.name: SQL Behavior Change After Upgrade
nodes.content: Statements that ran fine previously start erroring or returning different results after a version upgrade or migration, without any infrastructure fault.

nodes.name: Post-Migration SQL Semantic Mismatch
nodes.content: After migrating from Oracle or another database, application results silently differ or statements error: empty substring results, integer month differences, wrong date formats, or outer-join syntax errors that never appeared upstream.

nodes.name: SST File Corruption
nodes.content: Damaged SST files make a TiKV store panic (immediately before v6.1.0, or about an hour after detection since then), threatening region availability.

nodes.name: Stale Read Anomaly
nodes.content: Stale reads degrade: miss OPS rises, reads fall back to strong reads, and TiDB warns DataIsNotReady for Regions whose safe-ts lags.

nodes.name: Stale Read Error
nodes.content: Stale-read queries fail with errors such as DataIsNotReady or return older data because region safe-ts or resolved-ts cannot advance.

nodes.name: Stale Read Complaints
nodes.content: Readers observe data older than what was just written, typically seconds behind, without any error: low-precision TSO or historical-read semantics are serving cached or snapshot versions.

nodes.name: Stale or Pseudo Statistics
nodes.content: Missing or outdated table statistics make the optimizer misestimate cardinality and pick degraded plans; auto analyze only fires after the modified-row ratio passes tidb_auto_analyze_ratio (default 0.5) inside its allowed time window.

nodes.name: Statement Priority Modifier Ineffective
nodes.content: LOW_PRIORITY / HIGH_PRIORITY / DELAYED modifiers on DML no longer change scheduling after resource control is enabled (v6.6.0+); workload priority must be expressed through resource groups, so statements run at unexpected priority when operators still rely on the modifiers.

nodes.name: Statistics Outdated
nodes.content: Plans degrade because statistics are stale: EXPLAIN shows stats:pseudo or large estRows/actRows deviation after data changes.

nodes.name: Store Down
nodes.content: A TiKV store stops sending heartbeats long enough to be marked Down, triggering cluster-wide replica rebuild traffic

nodes.name: Blue-Green Cutover Replication Lag
nodes.content: During migration cutover the changefeed must catch up to the old-cluster up-tso after traffic is frozen; if GC lifetime is shorter than the backup/restore/upgrade/replication window, incremental replication enters an unrecoverable failed state and the whole migration restarts from a new full backup.

nodes.name: System Table Restore Incompatible
nodes.content: A BR restore of mysql-schema system tables fails or is skipped when the target cluster privilege tables are incompatible with the backup data (different table set, column count, column length, or ENUM value set).

nodes.name: TiCDC Changefeed Stalled or Failed
nodes.content: A TiCDC changefeed leaves RUNNING: WARNING means recoverable errors with continuous auto-retry while blocking GC; FAILED means replication cannot resume automatically and must be manually resumed before the incremental data is garbage-collected.

nodes.name: TiCDC CheckpointTS Stalled
nodes.content: A changefeed's CheckpointTS stops advancing or stays behind ResolvedTS, often after a capture restart such as an OOM kill, with the sink either lagging normally or blocked by a TiKV transaction or MVCC lock.

nodes.name: TiCDC Sink Backpressure
nodes.content: The downstream write path loses capacity because of table-bound work such as triggers even when TiDB, TiKV, PD, and the changefeed control plane are healthy.

nodes.name: TiCDC Sink Failure
nodes.content: The changefeed's downstream fails: Kafka broken pipe or EOF, oversized message rejection, or MySQL sink timezone and DDL errors.

nodes.name: TiCDC Stale Service GC Safepoint
nodes.content: An abandoned TiCDC changefeed leaves a PD service GC safepoint owner that pins the effective oldest safe point after the capture stopped, blocking GC progress and accumulating MVCC versions.

nodes.name: TiDB Memory Flow Control
nodes.content: When a SQL execution exceeds tidb_mem_quota_query with tidb_enable_rate_limit_action enabled, TiDB stops operator read threads one by one, throttling the query; the log line 'memory exceeds quota, destroy one token now' marks this state.

nodes.name: TiDB Memory Abnormal
nodes.content: TiDB process memory usage rises abnormally close to its limit, risking OOM or aggressive session termination.

nodes.name: TiDB OOM / Memory Quota Exceeded
nodes.content: tidb-server process memory exhaustion or per-query memory quota violation; manifests as 'Out Of Memory Quota' errors, OOM kills of the process, or memory alarm logs.

nodes.name: TiFlash Analytic Overload
nodes.content: TiFlash serves analytical requests under a practical concurrency ceiling (typically below ~100 QPS depending on data volume and query complexity), and large INSERT INTO SELECT materialization statements hit memory quota or transaction size limits; strict sql_mode also prevents the SELECT subquery of INSERT INTO SELECT from being pushed down to TiFlash.

nodes.name: TiFlash Data File Corruption
nodes.content: A TiFlash node's data files become corrupted and the node cannot serve replicas correctly; the documented repair path is taking the node down, deleting its data, and redeploying it so replicas are rebuilt from scratch.

nodes.name: TiFlash Node Memory Exhaustion
nodes.content: Large hash joins, hash aggregations, or sorts push single TiFlash nodes to tens of GiB of peak memory (MemoryTracker) and risk node OOM when no operator-level or query-level spill thresholds are set.

nodes.name: TiFlash Query Error
nodes.content: Queries routed to TiFlash fail or fall back unexpectedly, often with errors from the columnar engine or its disaggregated mode configuration.

nodes.name: TiFlash Disaggregated Remote Read Slowness
nodes.content: Under the TiFlash disaggregated architecture, queries slow down when Compute-Node local SSD caches miss and data must be fetched from Write Nodes or S3 object storage.

nodes.name: TiFlash Replica Issue
nodes.content: TiFlash replicas stay unavailable, never appear after SET TIFLASH REPLICA, replication stalls or slows, or queries hit Region Unavailable under heavy TiFlash load.

nodes.name: TiFlash Restart Failure After Version Change
nodes.content: TiFlash upgrades convert on-disk formats (RocksDB, PageStorage V3, DTFile versions), so a downgraded TiFlash may fail to parse newer files and cannot restart; online upgrade of old TiFlash versions also requires a stop-first procedure with matching TiUP versions.

nodes.name: TiFlash Node Removal Stuck
nodes.content: Scale-in of TiFlash nodes stalls when surviving tables request more TiFlash replicas than remaining nodes (PD refuses to move peers off the leaving nodes) or when replication rules of recently dropped tables still exist in PD until GC completes.

nodes.name: TiFlash Query Fallback
nodes.content: Analytical queries expected to run on TiFlash MPP stay slow because the statement contains operators or functions unsupported in MPP mode, or TiFlash-friendly optimizations are disabled, so the query falls back or reads far more data than needed.

nodes.name: TiKV Thread CPU Saturation
nodes.content: A TiKV thread pool (gRPC, scheduler, raftstore, apply, or coprocessor) runs at its utilization ceiling, capping throughput and inflating latency while other resources stay idle.

nodes.name: TiKV Disk Space Pressure
nodes.content: When remaining disk space falls below the reserved protection space (default 5 GiB), TiKV restricts writes; after actual exhaustion TiKV goes offline and restarts only after space is reclaimed.

nodes.name: TiKV OOM
nodes.content: TiKV repeatedly hits Out of Memory, most often because the RocksDB block cache (40% of system memory by default) plus multiple TiKV instances on one host exceed physical memory.

nodes.name: TiKV Overload
nodes.content: TiKV saturates CPU or disk I/O and applies backpressure: logs show 'Server is busy', backoff maxsleep, or channel full, and Region leaders flap between stores.

nodes.name: TiKV Startup Failure
nodes.content: TiKV exits at startup with 'cluster ID mismatch' (local data belongs to a different PD cluster) or 'duplicated store address' (the address is still registered in PD from a previous store).

nodes.name: TiKV Storage Space Amplification
nodes.content: TiKV disk usage grows faster than the logical data size, eventually threatening disk exhaustion on storage nodes.

nodes.name: TiKV Write Throttle (ServerIsBusy)
nodes.content: TiKV throttles or rejects foreground writes with ServerIsBusy when kvDB memtable count, L0 file count, or pending compaction bytes exceed flow-control limits (soft 192 GiB / hard 1024 GiB), or when the scheduler write queue passes scheduler-pending-write-threshold (100 MiB).

nodes.name: Timeout and GC Errors
nodes.content: Statements or transactions fail with timeout errors: GC life time exceeded by transaction duration, transaction TTL rollback, idle-transaction termination, or client/JDBC query timeout.

keywords: GC life time is shorter than transaction duration

nodes.name: Titan Space Amplification
nodes.content: With the Titan blob engine enabled, disk usage grows from space amplification and Titan GC competes with foreground writes, hurting write latency and range scans.

nodes.name: Replica Placement Violations
nodes.content: Replicas cluster on the same host, rack, or zone - or cannot be placed at all - because PD location-labels, isolation-level, TiKV labels, or placement rules disagree.

nodes.name: High TSO RPC Latency
nodes.content: Query latency rises with elevated TSO wait times: the PD leader CPU is bottlenecked by high TSO request pressure, or the path to PD is network-degraded.

nodes.name: TSO Service Unavailable
nodes.content: PD stops allocating timestamps (leader loss, etcd quorum loss or overload), so all transactions stall cluster-wide

nodes.name: TSO Wait Duration Rise
nodes.content: The PD TSO wait duration metric (expected under 50ms) climbs abnormally, stretching every transaction's start-timestamp allocation.

nodes.name: TTL Cleanup Backlog
nodes.content: Expired rows accumulate when TTL deletion rate stays below insertion rate or TTL jobs never run: table-level TTL_ENABLE='OFF', global tidb_ttl_job_enable=OFF, a schedule window that excludes the current time, or an unsplittable clustered-index table executing sequentially on one TiDB node.

nodes.name: TTL Cleanup Interfering with Workload
nodes.content: TTL background scan/delete jobs consume TiDB CPU and TiKV disk/CPU and can degrade online read/write latency during their schedule window.

nodes.name: Transaction Size Limit Exceeded
nodes.content: Writes fail when a single row exceeds the entry size limit or a transaction exceeds the total size limit, and downstream Kafka consumers can reject oversized binlog messages even though TiDB committed successfully.

nodes.name: Unexpected Stale Read
nodes.content: Applications observe outdated data or read-only errors because session or global stale-read controls (tidb_read_staleness, tidb_external_ts with tidb_enable_external_ts_read) are still enabled.

nodes.name: Unstable Query Results
nodes.content: Repeated executions of the same SQL return different row order or different rows because TiDB reads from multiple TiKV Regions in parallel and caches no data pages, so any query without a fully deterministic ordering or aggregation is exposed.

nodes.name: Upgrade Blocked by DDL
nodes.content: Upgrading while a DDL is running (pre-v7.1.0) or issuing DDL during an upgrade can cause undefined behavior; rolling updates also degrade traffic and require a minimum topology (TiDB x2, PD x3, TiKV x3).

nodes.name: Cluster Upgrade Failure or Stall
nodes.content: A rolling or offline cluster upgrade aborts or hangs when DDL jobs run during upgrade, the DXF is enabled during smooth upgrade, plugins load mid-upgrade, a node was killed -9, the DDL owner changes, leader eviction exceeds its timeout, or statistics loading exceeds the TiUP wait timeout.

nodes.name: Write Conflict
nodes.content: Concurrent transactions updating the same rows (especially under the optimistic transaction model) fail with write conflict errors (9007) or retryable commit errors (8002/8022/8028), surfacing as commit failures and application retries.

nodes.name: Write Hotspot
nodes.content: Write traffic concentrates on a single Region or leader (for example sequential auto-increment inserts), saturating one store while others stay idle.

nodes.name: Writes Rejected by Read-Only Mode
nodes.content: INSERT/UPDATE/DDL statements are rejected cluster-wide although the cluster looks healthy: one of the cluster-wide read-only switches is ON.

nodes.name: Write Stall
nodes.content: RocksDB or Raft Engine pauses foreground writes when flush, compaction, or WAL limits are hit, producing write latency spikes and client backoff.
